### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

Add a ggml backend for AMD XDNA NPUs (`ggml-xdna`).

  This would allow llama.cpp to offload compute operations (starting with matrix multiplications) to the Neural Processing Unit found in AMD Ryzen AI processors (Strix, Strix Halo, Krackan Point, and future XDNA3 chips).

  The backend would use AMD's XRT (Xilinx Runtime) C++ API to dispatch compiled NPU kernels (xclbin binaries), with compiled binaries cached on disk for fast subsequent runs.


### Motivation

AMD ships an NPU in every Ryzen AI laptop but there's currently no way to use it from llama.cpp. The existing options are:

  - **FastFlowLM** — closed-source, only supports ~35 pre-compiled models, no community extensibility
  - **AMD RyzenAI SDK** — ONNX Runtime based, not integrated with the llama.cpp/ggml ecosystem
  - **ggml-cann** — similar concept but for Huawei Ascend NPUs, not AMD

  An open-source ggml backend for XDNA would:
  - Unlock NPU acceleration for every GGUF model, not just a curated list
  - Let millions of Ryzen AI laptop users run local LLMs on their NPU
  - Follow the same pattern as ggml-cann (hardware NPU backend via vendor SDK)
  - Complement existing backends — NPU handles matmuls while CPU handles the rest, similar to ggml-blas but with dedicated hardware

### Possible Implementation

Architecture follows the ggml-blas pattern (host memory, offload compute-heavy ops):

  1. **Phase 1 — MUL_MAT only:** Backend claims `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` for large contiguous matrices. Compiles NPU kernels via IRON (open-source AMD NPU operator library, github.com/amd/IRON) and caches the resulting xclbin binaries at `~/.cache/ggml-xdna/`. Dispatches via XRT C++ API. All other ops fall back to CPU automatically.

  2. **Phase 2 — More ops:** Add activations (SiLU, GELU, ReLU), norms (RMSNorm, LayerNorm), RoPE, Softmax — all already available as IRON operators.

  3. **Phase 3 — Fusion pass:** Intercept `ggml_cgraph` in `graph_compute`, pattern-match common blocks (Norm→GEMM, GEMM→Activation, full SwiGLU FFN, GQA Attention), replace subgraphs with fused NPU kernels that eliminate xclbin switching overhead and keep data on-chip between operations.

  Dependencies:
  - **XRT** (Xilinx Runtime) — `/opt/xilinx/xrt/`, provides `xrt_device.h`, `xrt_bo.h`, `xrt_kernel.h`, links `libxrt_core.so`
  - **IRON** (github.com/amd/IRON) — Python-based operator compilation (design.py → MLIR → xclbin). Used at compile time only, not embedded at runtime.

  I have a working skeleton (compiles, links against XRT, registers as backend) and am working on the XRT dispatch implementation. Happy to submit a draft PR once MUL_MAT dispatch works end-to-end

Replace the fixed 8-token cutoff with the #25356 density gate (`n_tokens * experts_per_token <= 2 * n_experts`, capped at 64 tokens). Avoids the batch-9 decode regression on AMD RADV; validated on gfx1151, RDNA3 and gfx1013 (BC-250): +36% at B=9, +27% at B=16, +21% at B=64, neutral at B<=8.

Assisted-by: DeepSeek V4 Flash

## Overview

Replace the hardcoded `batch <= 8` threshold for the Vulkan `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID` MMV path with the routed-density heuristic proposed in #25356.

For MoE decode, the MMV kernel performs better for small routed workloads, while the tiled kernel wins at larger workloads. The fixed cutoff causes a sharp kernel-selection regression when going from 8 to 9 concurrent sequences on AMD RADV.

The new gate keeps MMV selected while:

```text
n_tokens * experts_per_token <= 2 * n_experts
```

and `n_tokens <= 64`.

The existing F32/F16/quantized type check is unchanged, and large-batch prefill remains on the tiled path.

## Additional information

On a BC-250 (`gfx1013`), the new gate produced:

* B=9: +36%
* B=16: +27%
* B=64: +21%
* B<=8: neutral
* PP512: neutral (303-304 t/s)

The same density heuristic has previously been validated on Strix Halo (`gfx1151`) and RDNA3 in the discussion of #25356.

Forcing the tiled path everywhere was also tested on `gfx1013` and performed substantially worse (-44% at tg64, about -50% at B=1), supporting kernel selection rather than removal of the MMV path.

The change is limited to `ggml_vk_use_mul_mat_vec_id()`: 9 insertions, 1 deletion, with no new configuration or environment knobs.

Correctness: `test-backend-ops -b Vulkan0 -o MUL_MAT_ID` passes `872/872`
on the patched build (gfx1013, RADV).

## Related work

- #25356: reports the same batch-9 performance cliff on Strix Halo and proposes the density-based heuristic used here.
- #25862: addresses Vulkan MoE behavior for 256-expert models and a RADV tiled-shader pipeline compilation stall. This has a different motivation and is complementary to this change.
- #24407 / #24408: Intel Xe group-GEMM MoE work; unrelated to this kernel-selection heuristic.
- #25918: merged ZenDNN grouped-GEMM work for mul_mat_id on CPU; unrelated to Vulkan selection.

## Repro 

Reproduction (llama-batched-bench, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, 4-node RPC):
  stock:  B=8 52.6, B=9 35.9 t/s   (cliff)
  patched: B=8 51.5, B=9 48.2 t/s  (+36%)


## Requirements

* I have read and agree to the [[contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
* AI usage disclosure: YES - DeepSeek V4 Flash was used to assist with analysis and drafting of the code change and PR description. The submitted change and validation were reviewed by the author.

items.body:
## Bug Description

GLM-5.2 crashes deterministically when attempting distributed inference across multiple DGX Spark nodes via ggml-rpc. The crash occurs during graph computation with `invalid data ptr` on the worker side and `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor` abort on the orchestrator side. This appears analogous to #26424 (DeepSeek V4, Metal) but affects CUDA (sm_121).

## Environment

- **Hardware:** 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, Grace Blackwell, 128GB unified memory each)
- **OS:** DGX OS (Ubuntu-based, aarch64)
- **CUDA:** sm_121 native build
- **llama.cpp:** master `5788b510a` (ggml 0.18.1), built with `-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON`
- **Network:** 1Gbit Ethernet between nodes
- **Model:** GLM-5.2 UD-IQ4_NL (also reproduced with UD-Q4_K_M), unsloth GGUF split files

## Setup

**Workers (3 nodes):**

```
./build/bin/ggml-rpc-server -c --host 192.168.1.XXX --port 50052
```

**Orchestrator (1 node):**

```
./build/bin/llama-server \
  -m ~/models/gguf/glm-5.2/UD-IQ4_NL/GLM-5.2-UD-IQ4_NL-00001-of-00009.gguf \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
  -ngl 999 -c 4096 \
  --tensor-split 1,1,1,1 \
  --rpc 192.168.1.121:50052,192.168.1.111:50052,192.168.1.128:50052
```

## Expected Behavior

Model loads across 4 nodes and serves inference (works with Gemma-4-26B, Qwen3.6-35B, Mistral-Small-3.2 on identical setup).

## Actual Behavior

Weights distribute successfully (~113GB cache per worker), but crashes during graph_compute:

**Worker output:**

[create_node] invalid data ptr[graph_compute] failed to create graph node 30 (id=197768091778640)
Client connection closed

**Orchestrator output:**

ggml-rpc.cpp:519: Remote RPC server crashed or returned malformed response
recv failed (bytes_recv=0, size_to_recv=8)

Stack trace: `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor` → `ggml_backend_tensor_copy` → `ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async` → `llama_context::graph_compute` → `llama_context::decode` (during `common_init_from_params`).

## Reproducibility

- 100% deterministic — same worker, same graph node (30)
- Reproduced with UD-IQ4_NL (~348GB) and UD-Q4_K_M (~434GB)
- Reproduced with `-c 4096` and `-c 131072`
- Reproduced with and without `--no-warmup`
- All 4 nodes on identical commit (`5788b510a`, fresh pull)

## What Works

- Single-node llama.cpp on same hardware (Gemma, Qwen, Mistral)
- 2-node llama.cpp RPC with smaller models (Gemma-4-26B, ~51.8 tok/s)
- GLM-5.2 on single-node (4×RTX 6000, Ollama, Note: Different machine! But same model GLM 5.2 UD-IQ4_NL)

## Related

- #26424 — DeepSeek V4 Flash RPC crash (Metal, similar MoE/MLA architecture)
- GLM-5.2 uses IndexShare and MTP/NextN layers — likely unsupported ops in RPC graph distribution

## Logs

Full orchestrator and worker terminal output, dmesg are attached.

[glm-rpc-orch.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708516/glm-rpc-orch.log)

[glm-rpc-worker3.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708521/glm-rpc-worker3.log)

[glm-rpc-dmesg-g3.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708525/glm-rpc-dmesg-g3.log)

items.body:
## Summary

On AMD gfx1151 / Vulkan / RADV, `llama-server` with `--spec-type draft-mtp` dies mid-**prompt** (`decode() failed: vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost`) at tens of thousands of tokens. The same argv with MTP off survives past 125k. A one-site diagnostic that **keeps MTP flags on** but skips `common_speculative_process` while no slot is `SLOT_STATE_GENERATING` also survives past 125k on both 1-seat and 4-seat topologies; generate still drafts.

This is not a checkpoint / `get_tensor` death (`--ctx-checkpoints 0`, this-boot `create_checkpoint=0` `get_tensor=0` `update_tgt=0`). It is not “Vulkan FA at 114k without MTP” on one seat (MTP-off 1×262144 finished 125948). It is the extra draft-context decode that `impl_draft_mtp::process` runs after every target ubatch on `!is_mem_shared` Qwen3.8.

`GGML_VK_MAX_NODES_PER_SUBMIT=1` is already set (the UMA submit-frequency workaround from #24872 / the turboquant fork). It is not enough.

## Name and Version

```
b10352-4dee52f82
Vulkan backend, llama-server
```

`/props` `build_info` = `b10352-4dee52f82`.

## Operating systems

Linux (AMD Strix Halo box).

## GGML backends

Vulkan (RADV).

## Hardware

- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (`gfx1151`), 128 GB unified LPDDR5X
- GTT pool 124 GiB (UMA frame buffer ~2 GiB)
- RADV / Mesa **last recorded 2026-08-16: Mesa 25.2.8** (not re-probed on the day of this write-up)
- Env on every arm: `GGML_VK_MAX_NODES_PER_SUBMIT=1`, `queue_preemption_timeout_ms=60000`

## Models

- `Qwen3.8-27B` UD-Q8_K_XL + `mmproj-F16` (Unsloth)
- Hybrid (`qwen35`-family): most layers recurrent, a minority full-attention. Qwen3.8 MTP is `!is_mem_shared`, so the draft context is a **separate** `llama_decode(ctx_dft, same n_tokens)` after the target ubatch.

## Problem description

With `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2`, long unique-prefix prefill dies in `vk::Queue::submit` during prompt processing:

```
radv/amdgpu: The CS has been cancelled because the context is lost. This context is innocent.
ggml_vulkan: device lost on Vulkan0
srv  update_slots: decode() failed: vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost
```

dmesg is a compute-ring timeout then reset (`ring comp_1.2.0` / `comp_1.0.1`), process **survives** as a zombie (`/v1/models` 200, later `/completion` 500).

Call site (b10352 `server-context.cpp` `decode()`, then `common/speculative.cpp` `impl_draft_mtp::process`): after every successful target `llama_decode(ctx_tgt, ubatch)`, `common_speculative_process` runs. On this model that is a second same-width draft decode. `--ubatch-size 1024` ⇒ a 1024-wide draft graph after every 1024-wide target graph, at rising `pos`. The outer `decode()` catch does **not** say which of the two `llama_decode`s threw; the A/B below isolates the extra one.

There is an in-tree TODO immediately above the call:

```
// TODO: avoid restoring the draft context and re-evaluating the drafted tokens when not needed [TAG_SPEC_AVOID_DRAFT_REEVAL]
//       for now, always re-evaluate for simplicity
```

## A/B (same box, same GGUF, same day)

Shared flags on every arm unless noted:

```
-ngl 999 --flash-attn on --ubatch-size 1024 --batch-size 2048
--cache-type-k q4_0 --cache-type-v q4_0
--cache-prompt --cache-reuse 256 --cache-ram 0 --ctx-checkpoints 0
--image-min-tokens 1024 --threads 16 --jinja
GGML_VK_MAX_NODES_PER_SUBMIT=1
```

Hop = `/completion` unique prefix, tokenized **~125948**, `n_predict=1`.

| Arm | MTP | seats (`-c` / `-np` / slot) | process() during prompt | last healthy n | result |
|--|--|--|--|--:|--|
| A | **off** (no `--spec-type`) | 1 × 262144 | n/a | **125948** | HTTP **200**, 992.6 s, 126.90 t/s, DeviceLost=0, `get_tensor=0` |
| B | **on** `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2` | 1 × 262144 | stock (every ubatch) | **55296** / 0.44 | HTTP **500** at t=6:16.751, `decode() / vk::Queue::submit`, this-boot `create_check=0` `get_tensor=0` `update_tgt=0` |
| C | **on** n-max 2 | 1 × 262144 | **skipped** unless a slot is `SLOT_STATE_GENERATING` | **125948** | HTTP **200**, 993.2 s, 126.81 t/s, DeviceLost=0. Skip log counts 1/16/32/48. Hop 2: `draft_n=6` accepted **2** |
| D | **on** n-max 2 | **4 × 262144** (`-c 1048576 -np 4`) | **skipped** as C | **125949** | HTTP **200**, 994.6 s, 126.64 t/s, DeviceLost=0. Same skip counts. Hop 2: `draft_n=6` accepted **2** |

Production 4-seat MTP-on **stock** process-every-ubatch (same argv as D, unpatched binary) died three times in the **114–117k** band (`n_tokens=114025`, `114688`, `116736`), same raise, same zero copy counters. Do not collapse the 1-seat 55k death into those 4-seat 114k deaths — same class, different CONFIG. Arm D is the 4-seat isolation: skip the extra decode and the 114–117k band is crossed.

After C/D hop 1, `begin()` warned `ctx_dft pos_max=-1` (the skip did what it said). Hop 2 was a short unique prompt, `n_predict=32`: generate still ran draft-mtp (`draft_n=6`, accepted 2). Accept is degraded vs a filled draft KV — expected with an empty `ctx_dft`, not a reason to drop `--spec-type draft-mtp`.

## Minimal diagnostic patch (not proposed as the final ship)

In `tools/server/server-context.cpp`, around the existing `common_speculative_process(spec.get(), batch_view)` after the target ubatch:

```cpp

    return s.state == SLOT_STATE_GENERATING;
});

### Operating systems

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-bench

### Command line

```shell
cmake -B build-vulkan -DGGML_VULKAN=ON -DGGML_HIP=OFF -DGGML_CUDA=OFF  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release . && \
cd build-vulkan && make -j
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./bin ./bin/llama-bench \
  -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q8_0 \
  -n 128 -p 0 -fa 0 -r 5

GGML_HIPBLAS=1 LLAMA_HIP_UMA=1 HIPCXX="$(hipconfig -l)/clang" HIP_PATH="$(hipconfig -R)" \
cmake -S . -B build-no-rocwmma -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DGGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=OFF \
cd build-no-rocwmma && make -j
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./bin ./bin/llama-bench \
  -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q8_0 \
  -n 128 -p 0 -fa 0 -r 5
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I iterated with Claud Opus 4.8 to discover the root configuration for this performance bug. The execution was performed and analysis confirmed by myself.  The text below was summarized and beautified by anthropic.  This issue is related but, imo, orthogonal to #24437

On AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151, Radeon 8060S iGPU, 128GB LPDDR5X-8000), the ROCm/HIP backend delivers substantially lower token-generation throughput than the Vulkan backend on the same hardware and model. Token generation is memory-bandwidth-bound, and HIP appears to be leaving a large fraction of available bandwidth on the table.

Observed throughput (clean llama-bench runs)
| Backend	| tg128 (t/s)	| Effective BW	| % of 256 GB/s peak |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ROCm/HIP	| 33.7| 	~101 GB/s| 	~40%|
| Vulkan | 	49.5	 | ~149 GB/s	| ~58% |

Token generation for this MoE reads roughly the active-parameter bytes per token (A3B ≈ 3B active params at Q8_0 ≈ ~3 GB/token, plus KV/overhead). Effective bandwidth is t/s × ~3 GB. Both backends run on identical hardware, so the ~1.5× throughput gap reflects HIP achieving a markedly lower fraction of peak memory bandwidth on a workload that is fundamentally bandwidth-bound.

Where the time goes
Kernel dispatch counts from rocprofv3 (for n=128) show tg is dominated by the Q8_0 matvec path:

mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8> — 45,279 dispatches
quantize_q8_1 — 45,279 dispatches (on-the-fly activation quantization paired with the matvec)
These two kernels are the expected hot path for Q8_0 generation and are the natural target for any bandwidth/throughput investigation on this backend.


Example llama-bench runs
```
cd build-vulkan
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./bin ./bin/llama-bench \
  -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q8_0 \
  -n 128 -p 0 -fa 0 -r 5
ggml_vulkan: Found 1 Vulkan devices:
ggml_vulkan: 0 = AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV STRIX_HALO) (radv) | uma: 1 | fp16: 1 | bf16: 0 | warp size: 64 | shared memory: 65536 | int dot: 1 | matrix cores: KHR_coopmat
| model                          |       size |     params | backend    | ngl |  fa |            test |                  t/s |
| ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | --: | --: | --------------: | -------------------: |
| qwen35moe 35B.A3B Q8_0         |  34.36 GiB |    34.66 B | Vulkan     |  -1 |   0 |           tg128 |         50.57 ± 0.83 |

cd build-no-rocwmma
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./bin ./bin/llama-bench \
  -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q8_0 \
  -n 128 -p 0 -fa 0 -r 5
ggml_cuda_init: found 1 ROCm devices (Total VRAM: 111616 MiB):
  Device 0: AMD Radeon Graphics, gfx1151 (0x1151), VMM: no, Wave Size: 32, VRAM: 111616 MiB
| model                          |       size |     params | backend    | ngl |  fa |            test |                  t/s |
| ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | --: | --: | --------------: | -------------------: |
| qwen35moe 35B.A3B Q8_0         |  34.36 GiB |    34.66 B | ROCm       |  -1 |   0 |           tg128 |         34.51 ± 1.02 |
```

Methodology note: rocprofv3 profiling is currently unusable on gfx1151

I attempted to measure achieved bandwidth and per-kernel timing directly, but rocprofv3 7.2.1 produces invalid data for the dominant compute kernels on this part, so the bandwidth figures above are computed from model architecture rather than measured. Specifically:

Hardware counters (FETCH_SIZE / WRITE_SIZE): the main tg kernels report 0 bytes. mul_mat_vec_q (45,279 dispatches) and quantize_q8_1 (45,279 dispatches) both show FETCH_SIZE = 0 and WRITE_SIZE = 0, which is physically impossible — these kernels stream the Q8_0 expert weights. Only __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer (model-load copies) and a few elementwise kernels report nonzero bytes.
Kernel-trace timing (--kernel-trace): the same kernels report 0.000 ms total duration despite tens of thousands of dispatches, and several kernels report negative durations (e.g. soft_max_f32 at −0.330 ms, ssm_conv_f32 at −0.015 ms), indicating corrupted per-dispatch start/end timestamps.
Requesting FETCH_SIZE and WRITE_SIZE together initially failed with error cod

items.body:
Verified on current master (tip ece963f) serving Qwen3.8-27B, and reproduced identically on a fork build; posting per the contribution guidelines as an issue with a reproducible red test.

**What happens:** the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` endpoint accepts `echo: true` + `logprobs: N` but returns logprobs **only for generated tokens** — the `logprobs.content` array contains exactly `completion_tokens` entries, never the prompt tokens. No error, no warning.

**Why it matters (measured):** every loglikelihood-based evaluation slices prompt-position logprobs out of the echoed array (lm-eval's `parse_logprobs` does `token_logprobs[ctxlen:-1]`). With generation-only content that slice is empty → every choice scores an identical 0.0 → **exact random-chance scores, silently**. We measured this end-to-end: arc_challenge 0.2433 (chance 0.25), winogrande 0.500, piqa 0.4933 — identical to four decimals across spec-decode on/off, because the scores never read real values. The same model through the chat lane answers the same questions at 0.96/0.835 (arc/wino) — the model is fine; the endpoint contract is the problem.

**Red test (single curl):**
```bash
curl -s http://localhost:PORT/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":1,"echo":true,"logprobs":3}' | jq '{prompt_tokens: .usage.prompt_tokens, logprob_entries: (.choices[0].logprobs.content | length)}'
# EXPECTED for echo semantics: logprob_entries == prompt_tokens + 1
# ACTUAL: logprob_entries == 1 (the generated token only)
```

**Ask:** either implement prompt-token logprobs when `echo: true` (the OpenAI contract), or reject `echo: true` explicitly instead of silently accepting it. The first option makes every loglikelihood eval framework work correctly against llama-server — a meaningful win for the local-eval ecosystem.

Evidence trail: our stack audit is public at https://github.com/KyaniteLabs/qwen38-27b-strix-halo (WAVE4 + VALIDITY-MAP ledgers) and the related tool-salience finding at https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/27165.

## Overview

Issue #27194: fuse UNARY(SIGMOID|SILU)+MUL on Vulkan to match CUDA.
CUDA also fuses SOFTPLUS; tests already cover SILU/SIGMOID/SOFTPLUS.

## Additional information

### Design:
- mul.comp param3: 0=plain, 1=sigmoid(b), 2=silu(b), 3=softplus(b)
- Host swaps so unary src is always B
- Adjacent fuse via num_additional_fused_ops at UNARY
- Deferred fuse if graph_optimize splits the pair
- graph_optimize: consecutive exception + pull MUL after UNARY

### Tests:
- Before/after Qwen3.8-27B Vulkan input-output tested with temp 0, seed 42.
- Hardware: AMD Radeon 8050S Graphics (RADV STRIX_HALO)

```
./build/bin/test-backend-ops -b Vulkan0 -o SILU_MUL,SIGMOID_MUL,SOFTPLUS_MUL
# 60/60 OK

./build/bin/test-backend-ops -b Vulkan0 -o MUL,SILU,SIGMOID,SOFTPLUS
# 115/115 OK
```

### Operating systems

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
./llama-server -m /home/user/Models/lmstudio-community/gpt-oss-120b-GGUF/gpt-oss-120b-MXFP4-00001-of-00002.gguf \
    -t 4 \

    --parallel 10 \
    --cont-batching \
    --jinja \
    --reasoning-format deepseek \
    --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort": "low", "reasoning_format": "auto"}' \
    --n-gpu-layers 999 \
    --swa-full \
    --flash-attn on \
    -b 2048 \
    -ub 2048 \
    --no-mmap \
    --cache-type-k q8_0 \
    --cache-type-v q8_0 \
    --cache-ram 0 \
    --cache-reuse 256 \
    --defrag-thold 0.1 \
    --temp 1.0 \
    --top-p 1.0 \
    --top-k 0 \
    --min-p 0 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8888 \
    --api-key "okokok"
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Summary

The UMA (Unified Memory Architecture) detection introduced in PR #17368 incorrectly identifies AMD APUs (such as Strix Halo) as UMA systems and limits the available GPU memory to system RAM's `MemAvailable`, ignoring the much larger TTM (Translation Table Manager) memory allocation that AMD APUs can utilize.

## Environment

- **Hardware**: AMD Strix Halo APU (gfx1151)
- **GPU Memory**: 96GB TTM allocation via kernel boot parameters
- **System RAM**: 32GB
- **OS**: Ubuntu Linux with kernel 6.14.0
- **ROCm Version**: 7.9.0
- **llama.cpp Version**: Latest master (commit 0a0bba05e)

### Kernel Boot Parameters
```
amdgpu.gttsize=98304 ttm.pages_limit=25000000 ttm.page_pool_size=12000000
```

## Problem Description

After PR #17368 (DGX Spark: UMA support), the `ggml_backend_cuda_device_get_memory()` function checks `prop.integrated > 0` to detect UMA systems. When detected as UMA, it reads available memory from `/proc/meminfo` instead of using `cudaMemGetInfo()`.

**The issue**: AMD APUs report `integrated = true`, but they can utilize significantly more memory than system RAM through TTM. In my case:
- System RAM available: ~27GB
- Actual GPU memory available via TTM: **96GB**

This causes the new `llama_params_fit` auto-fitting logic to incorrectly calculate that there isn't enough memory, resulting in:
1. Context size being reduced from 131072 to 4096
2. Model layers being offloaded to CPU unnecessarily
3. Significant performance degradation

## Logs

### Before patch (incorrect behavior):
```
llama_params_fit_impl: projected to use 64909 MiB of device memory vs. 98304 MiB of free device memory
llama_params_fit_impl: cannot fulfill margin of 1024 MiB, need to reduce device memory by 37767 MiB
llama_params_fit_impl: context size reduced from 131072 to 4096
llama_params_fit_impl: ROCm0 (AMD Radeon Graphics): 36 layers (21 overflowing), 27049 MiB used
```

### After patch (correct behavior):
```
llama_params_fit_impl: projected to use 64909 MiB of device memory vs. 98304 MiB of free device memory
llama_params_fit_impl: will leave 33092 >= 1024 MiB of free device memory, no changes needed
```

## Root Cause

In `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu`, the `ggml_backend_cuda_device_get_memory()` function:

```cpp
#if defined(__linux__)
    cudaDeviceProp prop;
    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&prop, ctx->device));

    bool uma_env = getenv("GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY") != nullptr;
    bool is_uma = prop.integrated > 0 || uma_env;  // <-- AMD APUs hit this

    if (is_uma) {
        // Uses /proc/meminfo which returns ~27GB instead of 96GB TTM
        if (ggml_backend_cuda_get_available_uma_memory(&available_memory_kb, &free_swap_kb) && available_memory_kb > 0) {
            *free = (size_t)available_memory_kb * 1024;
        }
    }
#endif
```

## Proposed Fix

Skip the UMA memory detection for ROCm/HIP builds, as AMD APUs with TTM can report accurate memory via `hipMemGetInfo()`:

```diff
-#if defined(__linux__)
+#if defined(__linux__) && !defined(GGML_USE_HIP)
     // Check if this is a UMA (Unified Memory Architecture) system
+    // Note: Skip this for ROCm/HIP - AMD APUs with large TTM allocations (e.g., Strix Halo)
+    // report integrated=true but can use much more memory via TTM than system RAM
     cudaDeviceProp prop;
     CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&prop, ctx->device));
     ...
-#endif // defined(__linux__)
+#endif // defined(__linux__) && !defined(GGML_USE_HIP)
```

## Alternative Solutions

1. **Environment variable override**: Add an env var like `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_UMA_DETECTION` to skip UMA detection
2. **TTM-aware detection for AMD**: Check `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_vram_total` or similar for AMD GPUs
3. **Compare reported vs actual**: If `cudaMemGetInfo` returns significantly more than `MemAvailable`, prefer `cudaMemGetInfo`

## Verification

With the proposed patch applied:
- `amd-smi` shows 65GB+ GPU memory usage (correct)
- Model loads with full 128K context
- All 36 layers stay on GPU
- No unnecessary CPU offloading

## Related

- PR #17368: DGX Spark: UMA support
- PR #17537: cuda: fix UMA detection on discrete GPUs

## System Information

```
$ amd-smi
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| AMD-SMI 26.1.0      ROCm version: 7.9.0                                      |
|-------------------------------------+----------------------------------------|
| 0000:c5:00.0    AMD Radeon Graphics |                          65XXX/98304 MB |
+-------------------------------------+----------------------------------------+

$ amd-ttm
Current TTM pages limit: 25000000 pages (95.37 GB)
Total system memory: 30.99 GB

$ cat /proc/cmdline
... amdgpu.gttsize=98304 ttm.pages_limit=25000000 ...
```

_No response_

items.body: This PR adds a new `--numa mirror` option which mirrors model weights to each Numa node on the system, and uses a thread-local var in the OMP threadpool to select the correct mirror copy local to the thread at runtime, to eliminate cross-socket traffic. Build instructions: ``` apt-get update apt-get install -y libnuma-dev libgomp1 cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-march=native" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-march=native" -DGGML_OPENMP=ON cmake --build build --parallel ``` To test: ```bash # No mirroring: ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ~/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf # Numa mirroring of model weights to every node: ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ~/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --numa mirror ``` Test system is a two-socket Xeon 6238R Cascade Lake, with 768GB of DDR4-2933 (6 channels per socket). Without `--numa mirror`: ``` developer@81ec6c6e6af6:/workspaces/llama-cpp-dbsanfte-dev$ ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ./.devcontainer/Qwen3-32B-Q6_K.gguf | model | size | params | backend | threads | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | ------: | --------------: | -------------------: | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | pp512 | 20.99 ± 0.01 | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | tg128 | 1.91 ± 0.00 | build: c665d3c9 (6468) ``` With `--numa mirror`: ``` developer@81ec6c6e6af6:/workspaces/llama-cpp-dbsanfte-dev$ ./build/bin/llama-bench -m . /.devcontainer/Qwen3-32B-Q6_K.gguf --numa mirror | model | size | params | backend | threads | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | ------: | --------------: | -------------------: | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | pp512 | 21.36 ± 0.11 | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | tg128 | 2.70 ± 0.00 | build: c665d3c9 (6468) ``` Intel PCM tool during mirror inference showing both sockets using local mem: There's still a bit of cross-socket traffic (5%) because only model weights are mirrored, not tensors created at inference time. I'll play with that, maybe mirroring those aggressively will help too, or maybe not. Right now anything created at inference time just gets set to live on Node 0.

items.body:
## Overview

**cuda: fuse MoE weighted expert reduction**

Fuses the MoE expert-combine tail on the CUDA backend into one reduction kernel, removing the intermediate tensor traffic between its stages.

After `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID`, the combine is a per-expert scale/weight multiply plus an ordered left-to-right `VIEW`+`ADD` chain that sums the `k = n_expert_used` experts. Those are logical nodes: the backend already fuses consecutive MULs/ADDs, so for the common top-k = 8 case it runs as **two physical `k_bin_bcast` kernels** (fused two-MUL + fused seven-ADD) with the full weighted-expert tensor `[n_embd, k, n_tokens]` written out and read back between them. This PR replaces that with **one kernel** that reads each expert row once and writes the `[n_embd, n_tokens]` result once:

```
dst[t,c] = sum_e ((experts[t,e,c] * expert_scale[t,e]) * weight[t,e])
```

The sum keeps the original left-to-right order. **The primary benefit is reduced global-memory traffic** (the eliminated intermediate tensor)

**Matching** is purely structural (op / shape / stride / view offset / add-chain / closure / aliasing) — never the quant or model. Two shapes: short (`experts * router_weight`) and long (`(experts * expert_scale) * router_weight`). The long form appears whenever a per-expert broadcast scale is applied before the router weight (e.g. the NVFP4 `scale_2` output scale, but the same graph slot can carry other scales); the matcher keys only on that second MUL's presence.

**Kernels:** unrolled templates for `k = 2..8`, one runtime-`k` kernel for `k = 9..15`, a `float4` path when `n_embd % 4 == 0` and aligned (scalar fallback), and an optional per-expert scale via a template flag. The `k <= 15` cap is `ggml_can_fuse_subgraph`'s 31-node limit on the long form (`2*k + 1 <= 31`); larger `n_expert_used` falls back.

**Correctness:** full-model WikiText-2 perplexity is unchanged (**5.8857 ± 0.03661**, on vs off) and `test-backend-ops` passes; the reduction keeps the original left-to-right order. Guards: `weights`/`expert_scale` are copied to scratch when they overlap `dst` (read while writing `dst`); fusion is skipped when `experts` overlaps `dst`; view offsets/strides and the add-chain are validated before fusing.

**Fallback / kill switch:** any unsupported top-k or failed structural/layout/closure/alias check leaves the graph unchanged and runs the per-op path. Enabled by default; `GGML_CUDA_MOE_WEIGHTED_REDUCTION=0` forces the reference path.

## Additional information


**Performance** — prefill `t/s`, default-ON vs `=0`, same binary, mean-vs-mean:

| Hardware | Model | Quant | pp2048 | pp8192 |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| RTX 5090 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | NVFP4 | +3.6% | +3.6% |
| RTX 5090 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | Q4_K_M | +4.1% | +3.9% |
| RTX 5090 | Gemma-4-26B-A4B | NVFP4 | +4.3% | +4.3% |
| DGX Spark (GB10) | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | NVFP4 | +5.4% | +5.4% |
| DGX Spark (GB10) | Gemma-4-26B-A4B | Q4_K_M | +7.1% | +6.2% |

**Testing** (both modes, same binary): `test-backend-ops` **13,178/13,178** pass; CTest **42/42** pass; CPU-vs-CUDA compared; WikiText-2 PPL identical **5.8857 ± 0.03661**; `llama-cli` output unchanged. CUDA backend only; no changes to weights or numerics.

### Name and Version

```
version: 9960 (a935fbffe)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000099 for Darwin arm64
```

Homebrew build, Metal backend.

### Operating systems

Mac (macOS 26.5.1, build 25F80), Apple M5, 24 GB unified memory.

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Ornith-1.0-35B-UD-Q3_K_M.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 262144 -np 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa auto --port 8080
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When a Metal allocation fails during init, the server logs the failure, logs that the
backend is unrecoverable, and then finishes starting up anyway. It prints `model loaded`,
binds the port, and answers `/health` with `{"status":"ok"}`. Every completion request
after that returns HTTP 500.

The per-request errors are reported correctly, so this isn't silent corruption. The
problem is that startup completes and `/health` reports ready for a process that can
never serve a request. Anything using `/health` as a readiness probe treats it as up.

I should say up front that `-ngl 99` disabled the auto-fit that would otherwise have
prevented this:

```
W common_fit_params: failed to fit params to free device memory: n_gpu_layers already set by user to 99, abort
```

So the OOM itself is arguably my own fault. The part I think is still a bug is what
happens afterwards — the backend reports itself unrecoverable and the server starts
anyway.

Steps:

1. Pick a context size where the allocation cannot fit. On a 24 GB M5 the Metal device
   reports 18186 MiB, and this model at `-c 262144` needs 19005 MiB. llama.cpp's own
   memory breakdown says so directly:
   ```
   cmn  common_param:   - MTL0    : Apple M5 (18186 MiB, 18185 MiB free)
   load_tensors:  MTL0_Mapped model buffer size = 15897.19 MiB
   llama_kv_cache:       MTL0 KV buffer size =  2720.00 MiB
   common_memory_breakdown_print: |   - MTL0 (Apple M5)    | 18186 = ... + (19005 = 15897 +    2782 +     325) +         398 |
   ```
   At `-c 65536` the KV cache drops to ~680 MiB and it fits.
2. Start the server with the command line above.
3. 15 `Insufficient Memory` errors during init, then the backend declares itself
   unrecoverable and the decode fails.
4. Server prints `model loaded` and `listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080`.
5. `/health` → 200 `{"status":"ok"}`.
6. Any completion request → 500, and the OOM count roughly doubles.
7. Re-run at `-c 65536` and the same model starts and serves normally.

### What I'd expect

Exit non-zero at startup, the way other unrecoverable init failures already do — a
quantized V cache without flash attention returns `nullptr` and the server refuses to
start (b9960 `src/llama-context.cpp:3518`; on master the same check is at `:3602`,
reworded to `quantized V cache requires flash_attn to be enabled`).

Failing that, `/health` should reflect it. It currently returns `{"status":"ok"}`
unconditionally once the model is marked loaded (b9960
`tools/server/server-context.cpp:4322`, master `:4448`); the only gate is the
server-state middleware, which fires solely on `!is_ready`.

### Relevant log output

Init (timestamps and log-level prefixes trimmed):

```
ggml_metal_synchronize: error: command buffer 0 failed with status 5
error: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)
   ... 15 occurrences ...
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
graph_compute: ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async failed with error -1
process_ubatch: failed to compute graph, compute status: -1
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
cmn  common_conte: llama_decode() failed: -3
srv  llama_server: model loaded
srv  llama_server: listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080
```

One completion request afterwards:

```
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
srv        decode: Compute error. off = 0, n_batch = 2048, ret = -3
srv    send_error: task id = 0, error: Compute error.
srv  update_slots: decode() failed: Compute error.
```

Observed from the client:

```
$ curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' localhost:8080/health
{"status":"ok"}
200

$ curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' localhost:8080/completion \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"prompt":"int add(int a,int b){","n_predict":20,"temperature":0}'
{"error":{"code":500,"message":"Compute error.","type":"server_error"}}
500
```

`Insufficient Memory` count: 15 after init, 28 after one request, 29 including shutdown.

### Notes

Reproduced on b9960 (`a935fbffe`). I haven't run master, but both relevant paths look
unchanged there: the init probe still treats a failed `llama_decode` as non-fatal and
continues (master `common/common.cpp:1576`, b9960 `:1497`), and `/health` is still
unconditional. Worth confirming against master before acting on it.

One model, one machine, Metal only. Speculative decoding was not involved
(`speculative decoding not supported by this context` appears in the log).

### Name and Version

### Description

I'm observing a reproducible VRAM memory leak when running DeepSeek V4 Flash GGUF with DSpark speculative decoding enabled. After each PP+TG (prefill + generate) cycle, VRAM usage increases by approximately **10 MB**, and this accumulation continues until the process eventually runs out of memory (OOM).

This issue does **not** occur with:
- Step 3.7 + DSpark
- Qwen3.8-27B + DSpark

Both of the above maintain stable VRAM usage across multiple cycles.

### Environment
- Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731 version) GGUF + DSpark
- Framework: llama.cpp
- Issue: VRAM leak, ~10 MB per PP+TG cycle

### Suspected Root Cause

I suspect this is a **Draft KV Cache leak** specific to the DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 model when used with DSpark. Specifically:

1. **KV cache positions** are written during every draft step but are **never compacted or properly reclaimed**, leading to continuous VRAM growth[reference:0]. A similar issue has been reported in related forks where "positions are written every tree step but never compacted," causing OOM under sustained traffic[reference:1].

2. **DSpark draft KV-cache group poisoning**: The DSpark draft model's KV cache is flagged as an "eagle group" (same as EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP/DFlash)[reference:2]. The multi-group cache-hit lookup requires **every** KV-cache group to report a nonzero hit for cache reuse to succeed — any single group reporting zero short-circuits the entire request's lookup[reference:3].

3. **Sparse and discontinuous draft KV**: DSpark's draft-layer KV is recomputed from the target model's real hidden state every decode step, meaning it has **no cross-request reuse value**[reference:4]. Its stored blocks are sparse and discontinuous (e.g., `[MISS, MISS, HIT, MISS, MISS]`)[reference:5], never satisfying the consecutive-hit window required for cache lookup[reference:6].

4. **"One-vote veto" effect**: This permanently poisons the AND-combination lookup for the entire request[reference:7], even though the model's real KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) independently have a working hit rate around 89%[reference:8]. As a result, the prefix caching mechanism is effectively disabled — every new request cannot reuse historical caches and must recompute and write new KV cache entries, causing VRAM to grow until exhaustion.

A similar fix has been proposed in vLLM where DSpark draft KV-cache groups are excluded from the cache-hit lookup poisoning mechanism[reference:9]. The same root cause likely applies to llama.cpp.

### Why Step 3.7 and Qwen3.8-27B Are Not Affected

These models likely have different DSpark implementations or KV cache structures that do **not** trigger this cache lookup conflict, allowing normal cache reuse and stable VRAM usage.

### Suggested Fix Direction

- Exclude DSpark draft KV-cache groups from the prefix caching lookup's "all-groups-must-hit" requirement, similar to the approach taken in vLLM PR #47891[reference:10].
- Alternatively, ensure DSpark draft KV cache positions are properly compacted or reclaimed after each generation cycle, as addressed in PR #23461 for draft/MTP resources.

### Additional Context

There have been related reports of DeepSeek V4 KV cache not being reclaimed on slot release, and DSpark-specific KV cache issues with offloading connectors[reference:13]. This may share a root cause with the hybrid-attention KV handling.

Please let me know if additional logs or reproduction steps would be helpful.

Thanks!

I am experiencing a reproducible VRAM memory leak when running the **DeepSeek V4 Flash** GGUF model (quantization: `UD-IQ3_XXS`, 104 GB) together with the **DSpark** draft model (`dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf`) on llama.cpp.

cmake -B build-vulkan -DGGML_VULKAN=ON -DGGML_HIP=OFF -DGGML_CUDA=OFF  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release . && \
cd build-vulkan && make -j
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./bin ./bin/llama-bench \
  -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q8_0 \
  -n 128 -p 0 -fa 0 -r 5

GGML_HIPBLAS=1 LLAMA_HIP_UMA=1 HIPCXX="$(hipconfig -l)/clang" HIP_PATH="$(hipconfig -R)" \
cmake -S . -B build-no-rocwmma -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DGGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=OFF \
cd build-no-rocwmma && make -j
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./bin ./bin/llama-bench \
  -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q8_0 \
  -n 128 -p 0 -fa 0 -r 5
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I iterated with Claud Opus 4.8 to discover the root configuration for this performance bug. The execution was performed and analysis confirmed by myself.  The text below was summarized and beautified by anthropic.  This issue is related but, imo, orthogonal to #24437

On AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151, Radeon 8060S iGPU, 128GB LPDDR5X-8000), the ROCm/HIP backend delivers substantially lower token-generation throughput than the Vulkan backend on the same hardware and model. Token generation is memory-bandwidth-bound, and HIP appears to be leaving a large fraction of available bandwidth on the table.

Observed throughput (clean llama-bench runs)
| Backend	| tg128 (t/s)	| Effective BW	| % of 256 GB/s peak |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ROCm/HIP	| 33.7| 	~101 GB/s| 	~40%|
| Vulkan | 	49.5	 | ~149 GB/s	| ~58% |

Token generation for this MoE reads roughly the active-parameter bytes per token (A3B ≈ 3B active params at Q8_0 ≈ ~3 GB/token, plus KV/overhead). Effective bandwidth is t/s × ~3 GB. Both backends run on identical hardware, so the ~1.5× throughput gap reflects HIP achieving a markedly lower fraction of peak memory bandwidth on a workload that is fundamentally bandwidth-bound.

Where the time goes
Kernel dispatch counts from rocprofv3 (for n=128) show tg is dominated by the Q8_0 matvec path:

mul_mat_vec_q<(ggml_type)8> — 45,279 dispatches
quantize_q8_1 — 45,279 dispatches (on-the-fly activation quantization paired with the matvec)
These two kernels are the expected hot path for Q8_0 generation and are the natural target for any bandwidth/throughput investigation on this backend.


Example llama-bench runs
```
cd build-vulkan
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./bin ./bin/llama-bench \
  -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q8_0 \
  -n 128 -p 0 -fa 0 -r 5
ggml_vulkan: Found 1 Vulkan devices:
ggml_vulkan: 0 = AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV STRIX_HALO) (radv) | uma: 1 | fp16: 1 | bf16: 0 | warp size: 64 | shared memory: 65536 | int dot: 1 | matrix cores: KHR_coopmat
| model                          |       size |     params | backend    | ngl |  fa |            test |                  t/s |
| ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | --: | --: | --------------: | -------------------: |
| qwen35moe 35B.A3B Q8_0         |  34.36 GiB |    34.66 B | Vulkan     |  -1 |   0 |           tg128 |         50.57 ± 0.83 |

cd build-no-rocwmma
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./bin ./bin/llama-bench \
  -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q8_0 \
  -n 128 -p 0 -fa 0 -r 5
ggml_cuda_init: found 1 ROCm devices (Total VRAM: 111616 MiB):
  Device 0: AMD Radeon Graphics, gfx1151 (0x1151), VMM: no, Wave Size: 32, VRAM: 111616 MiB
| model                          |       size |     params | backend    | ngl |  fa |            test |                  t/s |
| ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | --: | --: | --------------: | -------------------: |
| qwen35moe 35B.A3B Q8_0         |  34.36 GiB |    34.66 B | ROCm       |  -1 |   0 |           tg128 |         34.51 ± 1.02 |
```

Methodology note: rocprofv3 profiling is currently unusable on gfx1151

I attempted to measure achieved bandwidth and per-kernel timing directly, but rocprofv3 7.2.1 produces invalid data for the dominant compute kernels on this part, so the bandwidth figures above are computed from model architecture rather than measured. Specifically:

Hardware counters (FETCH_SIZE / WRITE_SIZE): the main tg kernels report 0 bytes. mul_mat_vec_q (45,279 dispatches) and quantize_q8_1 (45,279 dispatches) both show FETCH_SIZE = 0 and WRITE_SIZE = 0, which is physically impossible — these kernels stream the Q8_0 expert weights. Only __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer (model-load copies) and a few elementwise kernels report nonzero bytes.
Kernel-trace timing (--kernel-trace): the same kernels report 0.000 ms total duration despite tens of thousands of dispatches, and several kernels report negative durations (e.g. soft_max_f32 at −0.330 ms, ssm_conv_f32 at −0.015 ms), indicating corrupted per-dispatch start/end timestamps.
Requesting FETCH_SIZE and WRITE_SIZE together initially failed with error cod

### Name and Version

```
$ ./llama-cli --version
version: 0.1.0-dev (build 599, commit ad1de39)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Also observed on `4f31eed` and `6b4344e` (llama-server and llama-cli).

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

AMD Radeon 890M iGPU (gfx1150, RADV 26.1.2, Mesa), Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, 32 GB LPDDR5 unified with 16 GiB firmware VRAM carve-out + 32 GiB GTT aperture. Debian 13, kernel 7.1.3. Kernel params include `ttm.pages_limit=8388608`.

### Models

`Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf` + `mmproj-Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-F16.gguf` (also crashed with GLM-OCR Q8 + mmproj; the specific model does not appear to matter - the crash happens at projector load).

### Command line

```bash
./llama-cli -m Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-F16.gguf \
  --image ui.png -p "What is the dialog title?" \
  -ngl 999 -fa on --temp 0.1 -no-cnv -n 30
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

On this iGPU class, loading ANY mmproj-bearing model balloons GPU-side (GTT/TTM) allocations until the kernel's global OOM killer fires - **at projector load time, before any image is processed**. The process is killed within seconds; with other services resident, the OOM kill cascades (we observed two full-host watchdog resets before isolating it).

Clean single-process repro (no other GPU consumers; process wrapped with `choom -n 1000` so the OOM killer prefers it):

VmSize timeline from `/proc/<pid>/status` sampling:

```
0s VmSize=18184kB    VmRSS=7420kB
2s VmSize=4119524kB  VmRSS=150708kB
4s VmSize=32033928kB VmRSS=28652kB
```

Kernel (verbatim):

```
oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE,nodemask=(null),cpuset=...,global_oom,task_memcg=/system.slice/uit2-repro.scope,task=llama-cli,pid=77433,uid=0
Out of memory: Killed process 77433 (llama-cli) total-vm:33279112kB, anon-rss:4kB, file-rss:52kB, shmem-rss:0kB, UID:0 pgtables:1436kB oom_score_adj:1000
```

Note `total-vm: 33.2 GB` vs `anon-rss: 4 kB` - the memory is almost entirely driver-side, invisible to memory cgroups. We confirmed a `systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=6G` wrapper does **not** contain it (the OOM still fires as `CONSTRAINT_NONE` global; TTM/GTT kernel pages bypass the cgroup). With slower leak progression (CPU projector via `--no-mmproj-offload`) the driver log fills with repeated:

```
radv/amdgpu: Failed to allocate a buffer:
    size      : 1073741824 bytes
    alignment : 262144 bytes
    domains   : 4
```

(1 GiB GTT allocation attempts, `domains: 4`.)

For contrast: the identical artifacts + fixtures run cleanly on a discrete RTX 3090 (Vulkan not involved; CUDA) - this appears iGPU/GTT-specific.

Related prior art: #24626 (absolute per-device memory budget for `--fit` on UMA), #26447 (iGPU Vulkan device-lost at large contexts).

### Suggested fix / ask

Bound or chunk vision-context allocations on UMA/iGPU devices (or document a safe configuration for this class). As-is, every mmproj model is a potential host-crasher on Radeon iGPU systems.

---

*Disclosure: this report was assembled with AI assistance from measurements captured directly on the affected host (VmSize sampling script, kernel journal, RADV logs quoted verbatim above). All data points are from real runs, not generated.*

items.body:
## Overview

Fixes a regression after #24233, which restored HIP integrated GPU detection. On my AMD APU, this also made the ROCm host-buffer path available for HIP integrated GPUs. With that path enabled, prompt input appears corrupted: chat templates and system prompts can be ignored, and generated output becomes garbage.

This change keeps integrated GPU detection/reporting intact, but disables direct ROCm_Host compute on HIP integrated GPUs. The fix does not disable host-buffer exposure entirely, pinned buffers remain available to preserve functionality, while only the problematic direct compute path is blocked.

## Additional information

Tested locally on gfx1151 / RDNA3.5 APU with ROCm 7.14. The corrupted input/output issue is fixed with this patch.
The issue appeared in external harnesses like Pi and OpenCode. It can also be reproduced in the built-in web UI with a sufficiently large combined first input. For example, gemma-4-26B-A4B with 4676 tokens of context or more outputs `<unused49>` indefinitely. Other models can be way more resilient and their output starts by saying 'Based on the text provided, which appears to be a corrupted or "hallucinated" version of a Wikipedia article'.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - I used AI assistance to review and patch the relevant code. I tested and reviewed the final change myself.

### Name and Version

Environment

GPU: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics (Battlemage), 32GB VRAM
OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-22-generic (xe driver)
oneAPI / Level Zero: Unified Runtime over Level-Zero V2, 20.2.0 [1.15.38308+1]
llama.cpp commit: 7dad2f1a17d65b5e2034c277125bc9f97573a779 (build b9660, 2026-06-15) for the SYCL repro; current master built locally with -DGGML_VULKAN=ON for the Vulkan comparison run
Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE), Q4_K_M, GGUF

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
SYCL launch command

llama-server \
  --model Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --device SYCL0 \
  --ctx-size 32768 \
  --parallel 1 \
  --n-gpu-layers 99 \
  --jinja \
  --no-mmap \
  --reasoning-budget 0 --reasoning off

Env: UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1, GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_FLASH_ATTN=1, ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

**Summary**

When the underlying GPU resets an engine mid-job (kernel-level xe driver "Timedout job" / "Engine reset" — see companion kernel-level report, link TBD), the SYCL backend never detects it. The server hangs forever, busy-waiting in sched_yield() inside the Level-Zero adapter, with /health still responding but /slots and /v1/chat/completions timing out indefinitely. There is no log output at the point of failure and no way to recover short of SIGKILL.

By contrast, on the same hardware, same model, same kind of underlying GPU reset, the Vulkan backend (ggml-vulkan / Mesa ANV) correctly detects device loss and the driver returns VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST to the application. (llama.cpp itself doesn't catch this exception today and the process aborts — see note at the end — but the detection is correct, which is the point of this report: SYCL has no equivalent detection at all.)

We believe the root cause of the GPU reset itself is upstream of llama.cpp (kernel drm/xe driver / GuC firmware level — filing separately here > https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/xe/kernel/-/work_items/8390), but regardless of that root cause, the SYCL backend hanging forever instead of failing visibly is a real gap worth closing on its own.

**What's been ruled out (from earlier isolated testing against the SYCL server)**

A tools array present without being invoked — no hang
A single forced tool call — no hang, sub-1s
Six simultaneous tool definitions with a genuine call — no hang, sub-1s
Context size from 32768 up to 262144 — hangs occur across the whole range, no clear correlation with size
One hang occurred at only ~2,048 prompt tokens, partway through generation (not during prefill)

These rule out grammar-constrained tool-call generation and large-context prefill as the trigger in isolation. Root cause now appears to be a GPU/kernel-level engine timeout under sustained load (separate report filed against drm/xe), reproducible regardless of which backend is driving the GPU — this report is scoped specifically to SYCL's lack of any detection/recovery path for that event.

Ask

Does the SYCL backend have (or could it have) any equivalent to Vulkan's device-loss detection — checking Level-Zero/SYCL exception state or a result code after a submission/wait, rather than spinning indefinitely?
At minimum, a bounded wait with a clear error/log output on timeout would let an operator's process supervisor recover automatically, instead of requiring an external watchdog to detect a silent hang via a secondary symptom (/slots timing out while /health stays fast).

Happy to test patches — this reproduces reliably under real agentic tool-calling load (multiple times per hour), so turnaround on verification should be fast.

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

SYCL symptom: indefinite hang, no error

GPU power draw stays elevated (~98W) for the duration — confirms the GPU is actively spinning, not idle/crashed/waiting on I/O. gdb backtrace captured live while wedged, all threads idle except one spinning in the Level Zero adapter's USM memcpy path:

Thread 1 (LWP 25923) "llama-server":
#0  __GI_sched_yield ()
#1  ... libze_intel_gpu.so.1
...
#14 ggml_sycl_mul_mat_id(ggml_backend_sycl_context&, ggml_tensor*) () from libggml-sycl.so.0
#15 ggml_backend_sycl_graph_compute_impl(...)
#16 ggml_backend_sycl_graph_compute(...)
#17 ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async()
#18 llama_context::graph_compute(...)
#19 llama_context::process_ubatch(...)
#20 llama_context::decode(...)
#21 llama_decode()
#22 server_context_impl::update_slots()
#23 server_queue::start_loop(...)
#24 llama_server(...)

Notably: at the kernel level (dmesg -T), this exact PID (25923) has a corresponding entry showing the GPU driver itself reset the engine and declared the job timed out, before this backtrace was captured:

xe 0000:03:00.0: [drm] Tile0: GT0: Engine reset: engine_class=ccs, logical_mask: 0x1, guc_id=2, state=0x249
xe 0000:03:00.0: [drm] Tile0: GT0: Timedout job: seqno=4294967200, lrc_seqno=4294967200, guc_id=2, flags=0x20 in llama-server [25923]

i.e., the SYCL/Level-Zero stack is busy-waiting on a GPU job the kernel has already torn down. It never finds out, and never times out on its own.

Vulkan Crash:

items.body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
Adds support for MiniMax-M3, a 60-layer / 128-expert MoE (3 dense + 57 MoE layers) using MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA): a GQA block-sparse attention where a lightweight per-GQA-group indexer scores the visible causal context, max-pools the scores into 128-token key blocks, and selects the top-16 blocks (the query's local block is always force-included). The main attention then runs only over the selected blocks (16*128 = 2048 KV per query), independent of context length, so decode attention cost stops scaling with context.

Implements the architecture from the MSA paper (arXiv:2606.13392v2) and follows the transformers reference (modular_minimax_m3_vl) for the indexer construction, selection semantics, and RoPE. MTP heads are not present in the released weights. Vision support is a separate PR (#25113).

Note that MSA is not an optional speed optimization, as the model is trained with sparse attention, so block selection is part of the model's semantics. Running dense attention is an out-of-distribution approximation that degrades output quality. The dense path exists only as a fallback for configurations that can't run MSA.

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

### Implementation
Batch and decode implement the same block-scoring and selection semantics, block scores bs = maxpool_128(idx_q*idx_k^T + causal mask) plus a host-provided local-force bias (large positive bias on each query's local block), ranked together for top-k. Selection is per GQA group (4 indexer heads, one per group, shared across the group's 16 query heads).

Within each stream, the four GQA groups are mapped onto the FA mask's ne[3] broadcast dimension and executed in one grouped flash-attention call.

- Batch (n_tokens_per_stream > 1, ie. prefill): a small CPU op turns block scores into a block-level 0/-inf mask, then the token-level expansion and combination with the causal mask happens on the GPU, and masked FA runs over the full cache views.

- Decode (1 token per stream): batched top_k on the GPU, index arithmetic expands block ids to flat (token, kv-head) row ids, one ggml_get_rows each gathers the selected K/V/mask, and FA runs over just the 2048 gathered tokens. 

Multi-stream (--parallel N) is supported whenever the KV cache is per-sequence (so kv_unified is false). In that configuration each stream's slots are then position-aligned, which MSA's slot-anchored block selection requires. 

The indexer also needs its own per-layer key cache. It is allocated F32 on the same backend buffer as the main K/V cache. Context-shift is not supported, since shifting would desynchronize the index cache.

### Requirements and fallbacks

- Flash attention required. Both batch and decode call ggml_flash_attn_ext directly and assume the non-transposed V layout that llama.cpp only provides with FA on. FA off uses dense build_attn (no sparsity) with a one-time warning that output quality may be degraded. 

- Unified KV cache with multiple sequences (--kv-unified + -np > 1) would silently break block anchoring so it also falls back to dense with a one-time warning. 

### Limitations

- Block selection is anchored to absolute KV slots. Erasing a prefix or middle of a sequence's history (llama_memory_seq_rm of a partial range) breaks selection silently. Removing whole sequences, trimming the suffix and reusing server slots is fine.
 
- Main KV cache: F16/BF16 are tested. Quantized KV-cache types are not yet validated.

### Quantization

Quants should keep the indexer projections (index_{q,k}_proj) at high precision(F32 ideally) since they drive block selection, so quant error there changes which blocks are read (a discrete retrieval loss), unlike a value projection. The cost is ~1 GB and these are some of the highest-value tensors in the model.

### Conversion

GGUFs must be converted with this branch and must keep the indexer tensors, weights with the indexers stripped will not work. 

### Performance

My tested config is expert-offload  bound.  MSA decode is essentially flat with context (7.7 tok/s at 5k -> 7.67 at 62k), prefill is roughly ~420-480 tok/s at 62k with -b and -ub 2048. Compute buffer at -ub 2048 / 62k ctx is ~4.6 GiB.

### How to test

As mentioned GGUFs converted with this PR are necessary, other's will fail to load. You can either convert one yourself, or you can use [this](https://huggingface.co/Serpen/Minimax-M3-MSA-GGUF/tree/main/Q4_K_M) Q4KM one (graciously provided by @AesSedai). 

CUDA build assumed (`-DGGML_CUDA=ON`), but in theory other backends with flash_attn_ext support for head-dim 128 should work (dense fallback otherwise), ROCm/HIP, Vulkan, Metal untested, reports welcome.

- Feed a ~4k and a ~30k+ prompt and generate. Decode throughput should stay roughly flat with context (fixed 2048-KV budget).

- Multi-stream: llama-server --parallel 2 (or 4) with concurrent requests of different prompt lengths.

### Credits

The initial MiniMax-M3 scaffolding was based on work by @danielhanchen. The sparse-attention indexer, the unified batch/decode MSA graphs, the KV-cache index handling, FA gating, and multi-stream support in this PR are new work.

## Requirements

*Filed by Claude (Anthropic's assistant) on behalf of @elimisteve, who reviewed it before posting. All logs and line references were produced on his machine at commit `11924d4c1`. What I could not verify is stated explicitly below.*

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 547 (11924d4c1)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```
Commit `11924d4c17abc27383376a1ac6a24fa3e36c1c0c` (master, 2026-08-02).

### Operating systems

Linux (Xubuntu, kernel 6.14)

### GGML backends

CUDA (13.1), CPU

### Hardware

Intel Core i9-13950HX · 188 GiB DDR5 · NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada Generation Laptop GPU, 12 GB

### Models

`unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF`, `UD-Q4_K_XL` (native MXFP4 experts), 5 shards.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` fails to start on `deepseek4` with the **default** `-np -1` (auto), and starts
normally with an explicit `--parallel 1`. Nothing else differs.

Auto mode is an unconditional `n_parallel = 4, kv_unified = true`
(`tools/server/server.cpp:151`):

```cpp
if (params.n_parallel < 0) {
    params.n_parallel = 4;
    params.kv_unified = true;
}
```

Under `kv_unified`, `n_ctx_seq` is deliberately **not** divided
(`src/llama-context.cpp:287`):

```cpp
if (cparams.kv_unified) {
    cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx;      // 131072
} else {
    cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx / cparams.n_seq_max;
```

Both values reach the dsv4 cache (`src/llama-model.cpp:2259-2268`) — `cparams.kv_unified`
(true) and `cparams.n_ctx_seq` (undivided).

`llama_kv_cache_dsv4` then **discards the unified flag**
(`src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp:1041-1053`):

```cpp
GGML_UNUSED(unified);

// Keep DSV4 KV/state streams per sequence even when public KV mode is unified.
const bool unified_raw = false;

kv_raw = std::make_unique<llama_kv_cache_iswa>(
        model, hparams_raw, type_k, type_v,
        v_trans, offload, swa_full, unified_raw, kv_size, n_seq_max, n_ubatch, n_pad,
        nullptr, filter_raw, reuse, nullptr);
```

`kv_size` is the constructor parameter received at line 1021 and is forwarded here
unchanged — it is not divided anywhere in between. Downstream, `n_stream` becomes
`n_seq_max` (`src/llama-kv-cache.cpp:82`):

```cpp
n_seq_max(n_seq_max), n_stream(unified ? 1 : n_seq_max), ...
```

So dsv4 combines the **non-unified stream layout** (`n_stream = n_seq_max`) with the
**unified sizing** (`kv_size = n_ctx`, undivided). Each mode is self-consistent on its own —
unified is 1 stream × `n_ctx`; non-unified is `n_seq_max` streams × `n_ctx/n_seq_max` — but
the combination appears to allocate `n_seq_max` streams of the *full* context.

The comment on line 1043 suggests forcing per-sequence streams is intentional for this
architecture. If so, the sizing may need to compensate.

#### Reproduction

Fails (default `-np`):
```
llama-server -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf \
  -ngl 999 --n-cpu-moe 43 --no-repack --load-mode mmap \
  --ctx-size 131072 -b 2048 -ub 512 -fa on -ctk f16 -t 8
```
```
E ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating 672.00 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E alloc_tensor_range: failed to allocate CUDA0 buffer of size 704643072
E llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: failed to allocate buffer for kv cache
E srv  llama_server: exiting due to model loading error
```

Succeeds — only `--parallel 1` added:
```
llama-server -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf \
  -ngl 999 --n-cpu-moe 43 --no-repack --load-mode mmap --parallel 1 \
  --ctx-size 131072 -b 2048 -ub 512 -fa on -ctk f16 -t 8
```

3/3 reproductions each way.

**Stronger isolation — `-ngl 0`**, which puts no model weights on the GPU at all and still
fails, at a much smaller context:

```
# -ngl 0 --ctx-size 32768, ~4.0 GiB free VRAM reported by nvidia-smi
default -np -1 : E ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer:
                 allocating 1290.30 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
--parallel 1   : I srv load_model: initializing, n_slots = 1, n_ctx_slot = 32768,
                 kv_unified = 'false'      -> starts normally
```

Note the failing 1290 MiB allocation is smaller than the ~4.0 GiB nvidia-smi reported free.
That figure is whole-GPU free memory with other resident processes (a browser compositor and
two small CUDA clients) on the same card, and it precedes the allocations this run had
already made, so it is not directly comparable to the failing request. The meaningful
comparison is the controlled one: same machine, same instant, same command, `--parallel 1`
succeeds and the default does not.

### What I could NOT verify

- **Exact byte counts.** The failing run aborts before printing the KV/compute breakdown, and
  this GPU has other resident consumers, so I have no clean side-by-side `KV self size`
  comparison. I am therefore **not** claiming a specific multiplier — only that the default
  path allocates enough more to fail where `--parallel 1` succeeds.
- **`--parallel 4` with `kv_unified = false`** (i.e. explicit `-np 4` rather than auto). That
  would separate "4 slots" from "unified sizing" as the cause. I could not run it in time;
  the code reading suggests it should succeed, since `n_ctx_seq` would then be divided. If a
  maintainer runs only one extra experiment, this is the one.
- Whether other architectures that similarly override `unified` are affected.
- Which fix is correct.

### Possible directions (untested — no PR proposed)

1. When the caller requested unified but dsv4 forces per-sequence streams, size each stream
   as `kv_size / n_seq_max` rather than `kv_size`.
2. Or mark `deepseek4` as incompatible with `kv_unified`, so `llama-context.cpp` takes the
   dividing branch and the existing non-unified math applies unchanged.

I have not built or benchmarked either, so I am not opening a PR.

### Workaround

Pass `--parallel 1` explicitly. This also leaves `kv_unified` at its `false` default, which
[#19523](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp

Note that llama-server --version on these images reports version: 1 (81a8712) — the fork stamps its own build number and commit, so the upstream base is identifiable only from the image tag (b10187 / b10207). Both builds reproduce identically. b10207 is ~20 upstream builds newer than b10187, so this is not a regression introduced in that window and not specific to the gfx906 fork. ### Operating systems Linux ### GGML backends HIP ### Hardware 6 × AMD Instinct MI50, gfx906:sramecc+:xnack- (0x66a1), 32 GiB each Uniform PCIe, 2 hops, all NUMA node 0, no XGMI Host: 8-core AMD CPU, 503 GiB RAM ### Models bartowski DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-MXFP4 — 4 shards, 145.63 GiB, 284.33 B params, arch deepseek4. Fully GPU-resident across all 6 cards. No CPU expert offload. deepseek4 is layer-split only on this backend (--split-mode tensor errors, row fails on gfx906). ### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Command line

llama-bench \
  -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-MXFP4-00001-of-00004.gguf \
  -ngl 999 -sm layer -mg 0 -ts 0.95/1.00/1.00/0.95/1.00/1.10 \

Problem description

Token generation is flat through depth 3072 and then collapses by 6.4× at depth 4096. Prompt processing degrades smoothly across the same range, with no corresponding discontinuity.

depth | pp512 (t/s) | tg64 (t/s) -- | -- | -- 2048 | 150.28 ± 14.07 | 15.61 ± 0.12 2560 | 150.93 ± 14.04 | 15.76 ± 0.16 3072 | 148.09 ± 12.95 | 15.78 ± 0.05 4096 | 123.67 ± 8.86 | 2.47 ± 0.03

  • 6-token prompt → tg 16.09 t/s
  • 7001-token prompt → tg 2.37 t/s (pp 196.03 t/s, unaffected)

https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF

Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B Q4_K_M (arch=qwen3moe, pure attention) — UNAFFECTED on both builds

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Newer qwen models 3.5+ hybrid models were outputing mostly gibberish and crashing.  I've tested most of these models previously and they were working. Honestly thought I did something at first but then realized it was just an update I'm guessing.

Two related symptoms affect all hybrid architecture models (identifiable by 
ssm_d_conv / ssm_d_state / ssm_dt_rank fields in print_info) on Intel Arc Pro B60 
using server-intel latest (built 2026-06-03). Both are fixed by pinning to b8477.

SYMPTOM 1 - CRASH (qwen3next arch, e.g. Qwen3-Coder-Next):
Model loads fully into VRAM then crashes during warmup mul_mat on SSM/GDN weights.
crash at ggml_sycl_op_mul_mat line:3093.

SYMPTOM 2 - EMPTY/GIBBERISH OUTPUT (qwen35 arch, e.g. Qwen3.6-27B/35B):
Model loads and generates tokens but "content" field in API response is empty or 
contains number spam (e.g. 03129816571033482510583...). All output goes to 
"reasoning_content" as corrupted tokens. On b8477 the same models produce clean 
coherent output in "content".

IMPORTANT CONTEXT - why this is hard to diagnose:
server-intel is a rolling latest tag. Not sure when build/image broke but when I tried most recent build or 2026-06-03 get the broken build. Same 
image tag, completely different behavior depending on pull date. At one point I randomly tested Coder-Next about a week ago and although slow it worked. Now I randomly couldn't get any model 3.5 or above to work without gibberish outputs .... Coder-Next had been working in earlier sessions, then 
silently broke when the image updated i'm guessing, I just can't pinpoint when, unless this is known already.

Pure attention MoE models (qwen3moe arch, no SSM layers) are completely unaffected 
on both builds and work correctly throughout.

Steps to reproduce (using Docker):

1. Pull latest server-intel:
   docker pull ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-intel

2. Run with dual Arc Pro B60:

   docker run --rm \
     --device /dev/dri:/dev/dri \
     --group-add 993 --group-add 44 \
     -e ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0;level_zero:1 \
     -e ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=1 \
     -e UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1 \
     -e GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_LEVEL_ZERO=1 \
     -e GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_VMM=1 \
     -e GGML_SYCL_DISABLE_GRAPH=1 \
     -p 8010:8010 \
     ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-intel \
     --model /models/Qwen3-Coder-Next-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf \
     --ctx-size 8192 \
     --host 0.0.0.0 \
     --port 8010 \
     -ngl 999 \
     --split-mode layer \
     --tensor-split 1,1 \
     --flash-attn off \
     --threads 1

3. For qwen3next: crash during warmup at ggml_sycl_op_mul_mat line:3093
   For qwen35: server starts, responds, but content field is empty or number spam

4. Replace image with server-intel-b8477 — identical command — both symptoms fixed

---

Side note for Ollama SYCL users:

This same regression affects users of https://github.com/eleiton/ollama-intel-arc
— an excellent community-maintained project providing native SYCL Ollama builds 
for Intel Arc GPUs. It is not a bug in that project. Ollama 0.30.2 pins 
LLAMA_CPP_VERSION=b9479 (confirmed via 
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/v0.30.2/LLAMA_CPP_VERSION) which 
pulls the broken llama.cpp commit via FetchContent at build time.

Workaround: add this to ollama-sycl/Dockerfile after WORKDIR /ollama, then rebuild:

    RUN echo "ec2b787eb" > LLAMA_CPP_VERSION

Once this regression is fixed in llama.cpp master, Ollama SYCL builds will 
automatically pick up the fix.

### First Bad Commit

Working: server-intel-b8477 (ec2b787eb), image built 2026-03-23
Broken:  server-intel latest (~b9479), image built 2026-06-03

Regression window: somewhere between 2026-03-23 and 2026-06-03.
llama.cpp ships multiple builds per day so this window contains 
hundreds of commits. Have not bisected further.

A git bisect focusing on changes to ggml/src/ggml-sycl/ggml-sycl.cpp 
around the ggml_sycl_op_mul_mat function (line ~3093 in broken build) 
would likely narrow it down quickly.

Related: #21474 (same crash class on iGPU/Meteor Lake — that reporter 
also identified b8477 as working)  I just used this image to see if it would work, and it did!

## Bug Description

Gemma 4 models generate an infinite stream of `<unused>` tokens (Token ID 14 = `<unused8>`) on the **Vulkan backend**, both with GPU offloading and CPU-only. No valid text is produced — the model runs until MaxTokens is exhausted.

This happens **despite** having all known Gemma 4 fixes applied:
- Tokenizer fix (#21343)
- Template parser fix (#21326)
- Custom newline split (#21406)
- Byte token handling (#21488)
- Logit softcapping (#21390)
- **Plus** the F32 MoE precision patch from PR #21506 (manually applied)

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26100)
- **GPU:** NVIDIA (24 GB VRAM), Vulkan backend
- **llama.cpp:** Built from `94ca829b6` (master, 2026-04-06) + PR #21506 patch
- **Model:** `gemma-4-E2B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf` from [unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF)
- **Build:** CMake + MSVC + `GGML_VULKAN=ON`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build llama.cpp from current master with Vulkan enabled
2. Load `gemma-4-E2B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf` with `-ngl 99`
3. Send any prompt (e.g., "Hello")
4. Observe: model generates ~18000+ tokens of `<unused8>` (token id=14) without producing any readable text or hitting EOG

## Diagnostic Data

Token sampling output (first 10 tokens):
```
Token[0] id=14
Token[1] id=14
Token[2] id=14
Token[3] id=14
Token[4] id=14
Token[5] id=14
Token[6] id=14
Token[7] id=14
Token[8] id=14
Token[9] id=14
```

Token 14 in Gemma 4 vocab = `<unused8>`.

Generation stats: 183 tok/s, 18432 tokens generated, 44.7 seconds — no EOG token emitted.

## Additional Testing

- **CPU-only (`-ngl 0`):** Same result — generates `[multimodal]` tokens (id=5) in an infinite loop. Also broken.
- **PR #21506 applied (F32 MoE FFN precision):** No improvement on either CPU or Vulkan.
- **Ollama:** Same model works correctly in Ollama (which uses its own llama.cpp fork), producing valid responses.

## Init Logs (successful)

```
Model handle: OK
Vocab size: 262144
Layers: 35
Context size: 32768
Gemma tokens: start_of_turn=105, end_of_turn=106, bos=2
System tokens: 11
Initialization complete!
```

Model loads correctly, context/sampler/batch all initialized — the issue is purely in inference/sampling.

## Related Issues

- #21321 — Gemma 4 generates `<unused24>` tokens (CUDA, partially fixed by #21506)
- #21343 — Gemma 4 tokenizer fix (merged, applied here)
- #21506 — F32 MoE precision (open, manually applied, does not fix this)

The root cause may be Vulkan-specific numerical precision issues beyond what #21506 addresses, or a different code path in the Vulkan compute shaders.

There are several issues about abnormal output in multiple GPUs case, like: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/23612. After disable dev2dev memcpy by L0 API, all issues disappear. This PR is used to fix them. This PR use SYCL API to implement dev2dev memcpy directly for dGPU+dGPU case. It should be quicker than host forward mode, and has same performance of L0 API as the test result. For iGPU+dGPU case, still use host forward mode. Add running time environment variable GGML_SYCL_DEV2DEV_MEMCPY to choose the SYCL or L0 API in dev2dev memory copy. Value:
* 0: SYCL API (default)
* 1: L0 API -- L0 API is found to lead to abnormal crash in some case. This debug flag is used to check the issue. The performance of two APIs are not obvious difference on two Arc770 cases: ``` ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ../models/llama-2-7b.Q4_0.gguf | model | size | params | backend | ngl | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | --: | --------------: | -------------------: | | llama 7B Q4_0 | 3.56 GiB | 6.74 B | SYCL | -1 | pp512 | 589.00 Â± 1.10 | | llama 7B Q4_0 | 3.56 GiB | 6.74 B | SYCL | -1 | tg128 | 60.96 Â± 0.05 | export GGML_SYCL_DEV2DEV_MEMCPY=1 ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ../models/llama-2-7b.Q4_0.gguf | model | size | params | backend | ngl | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | --: | --------------: | -------------------: | | llama 7B Q4_0 | 3.56 GiB | 6.74 B | SYCL | -1 | pp512 | 588.52 Â± 1.21 | | llama 7B Q4_0 | 3.56 GiB | 6.74 B | SYCL | -1 | tg128 | 60.88 Â± 0.03 | ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ../models/Qwen3.5-27B-Q8_0.gguf | model | size | params | backend | ngl | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | --: | --------------: | -------------------: | | qwen35 27B Q8_0 | 26.62 GiB | 26.90 B | SYCL | -1 | pp512 | 159.71 Â± 0.14 | | qwen35 27B Q8_0 | 26.62 GiB | 26.90 B | SYCL | -1 | tg128 | 9.50 Â± 0.00 | export GGML_SYCL_DEV2DEV_MEMCPY=0 ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ../models/Qwen3.5-27B-Q8_0.gguf | model | size | params | backend | ngl | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | --: | --------------: | -------------------: | | qwen35 27B Q8_0 | 26.62 GiB | 26.90 B | SYCL | -1 | pp512 | 159.54 Â± 0.24 | | qwen35 27B Q8_0 | 26.62 GiB | 26.90 B | SYCL | -1 | tg128 | 9.50 Â± 0.00 | ```
