items.body:
## Summary

On Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage G31, 32 GB, 608 GB/s), token-generation
speed collapses with context depth far beyond what KV-cache bandwidth can
explain. The excess cost is a near-constant **~21-25 ns per KV position per
full-attention layer per token**, and it is invariant across:

- **backend**: Vulkan (Mesa 26.1.6 ANV) and SYCL (oneAPI 2025.3, L0 V2) pay the same tax;
- **model/geometry**: hybrid Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (2 KV heads × hs256), Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B (4 × hs128), Gemma 4 26B-A4B / 12B (8 × hs512) — KV row width 1 KiB vs 8 KiB makes no difference;
- **build**: b8183 and b10235 behave identically at depth;
- **quantization**: Q2_K vs Q4_K_M identical depth deltas.

Byte-independence rules out DRAM bandwidth. The signature fits
memory-latency-bound attention matvecs: too few outstanding loads to cover
GDDR6 latency. Supporting evidence: GPU holds max clock at its power cap
while useful traffic is a fraction of peak; running 4 concurrent streams
scales aggregate throughput ~2.4× (parallel streams supply the MLP a single
stream lacks); the same llama.cpp code on an AMD Strix Halo iGPU with less
than half the bandwidth holds the sibling model flat to 65k
(https://lilting.ch/en/articles/qwen35-ctx-kv-cache-vulkan-optimization).

## Environment

- GPU: Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB (PCI 8086:e223), PCIe passthrough to a Linux VM (6 vCPU, 16 GB RAM). d0 results match published bare-metal numbers, and all depth effects are on-card, so virtualization is not a factor.
- Host driver: xe, kernel 6.17; Vulkan: Mesa 26.1.6 (kisak), KHR_coopmat active; SYCL: oneAPI 2025.3 image, compute runtime 26.18.
- llama.cpp b10235 (also tested b8183), Vulkan and SYCL builds, `-ngl 999 -ub 512 -fa 0 -n 256 -p 0 -r 1 -d <depth>`.

## Data (tg256, t/s)

| model | backend | d0 | d32k | d65k | d127k |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M (hybrid, 10 attn layers) | Vulkan | 70.7 | 58.4 | 32.2 | 20.7 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q2_K | Vulkan | 72.0 | 60.2 | 33.4 | 21.2 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q2_K | SYCL | 81.5 | 52.9 | 38.5 | 22.8 |
| Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B Q4 (48 attn layers) | Vulkan b10235 | 87.1 | 37.6 | ~11-13 | |
| Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B Q4 | Vulkan b8183 | 103.7 | 35.8 | | |
| Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B Q4 | SYCL | 105.9 | 20.5 | 11.2 | |
| Gemma 4 26B-A4B Q4 | Vulkan | 69.2 | 57.8 | 30.9 | |
| Gemma 4 12B Q4 | Vulkan | 48.4 | 31.7 (d32k) | 22.5 | |
| Gemma 4 12B Q4 | SYCL | 51.8 | 34.8 (d32k) | 25.3 | |

Per-token excess over each model's own d0 baseline, divided by
(n_kv × full-attention layers), lands at 21-25 ns for every row above
(Gemma global-layer counts estimated from sliding_window_pattern).

Physics reference: Qwen3.6's KV is only 20 KiB/token (10 attn layers × 2 KV
heads × 256 × 2 × f16; 30 of 40 layers are DeltaNet with fixed state), i.e.
2.6 GB at 127k — ~5 ms/token at realistic bandwidth. Measured excess: ~33 ms.

## Control: same card, same model, different kernels — no depth tax

Intel's own stack (intel/llm-scaler-vllm 0.21.0-b2, vLLM v0.21.1 XPU, same
B70, same Qwen3.6-35B-A3B as GPTQ-Int4) decodes **flat to 127k**:

| depth | llama.cpp Vulkan b10235 (Q4_K_M) | vLLM XPU (GPTQ-Int4) |
|---|---|---|
| ~0 | 70.7 | 18.8-22.4 |
| 32k | 58.4 | 22.6 |
| 65k | 32.2 | 18.3-22.5 |
| 127k | 20.7 | 16.2-21.8 |

vLLM XPU's baseline is ~3.5× lower (eager GPTQ-MoE kernels), but its depth
cost is ~zero — demonstrating the Xe2 hardware itself can serve 127k
context with no per-position penalty. The tax measured above is specific to
ggml's decode-attention kernels.

## Additional findings from the same investigation

1. **Silent CPU fallback** (gdb-verified): with fa off, when the prefill
   score tensor (n_kv × n_ubatch × n_heads × 4B) exceeds free VRAM, the
   scheduler reroutes the matmul to the CPU backend with no warning —
   ~100× slowdown that presents as a hang. A log line when an op planned
   for GPU falls back would save users days. Likely the mechanism behind
   #18808's "almost stops".
2. **`-ctk q8_0` with fa off** also silently falls back to CPU on Vulkan.
3. **SYCL cannot load models whose weight buffer exceeds ~16.5 GiB**
   (`ggml_backend_sycl_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: can't allocate ... on
   device`, 29 GiB free): the SYCL backend allocates weights as one buffer
   and get_max_size does not reflect the device's real single-allocation
   ceiling; the Vulkan backend chunks. Qwen3.6-35B Q4_K_M (19.6 GiB)
   cannot run on SYCL on a 32 GB card. UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS,
   NEOReadDebugKeys/AllowUnrestrictedSize, legacy L0 adapter: no effect.
4. **b8183 → b10235 regressed MoE decode d0 ~19% on Vulkan**
   (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B: 103.7 → 87.1 tg256).
5. fa=on is uniformly slower than fa=off on Xe2 for tg at every depth
   (Qwen3.6: 68.5/32.1/20.8/12.5 vs 70.7/58.4/32.2/20.7), q8_0 KV does not
   close the gap.

## Ask

The per-position constant suggests the decode-path attention matvec kernels
(both backends) issue too few concurrent loads on Intel to hide memory
latency at large n_kv. Happy to run diagnostics/patches on this hardware —
single-owner box, can bisect or profile on request.

### Name and Version


version: 9197 (0443f8906) 
built with MSVC 19.44.35227.0 for Windows AMD64
main branch with #23174 merged

### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-cli

### Command line

```shell
.\llama-cli.exe `
  -m ".gguf" `
  --ctx-size 16384 `
  --n-gpu-layers auto `
  --flash-attn on `
  --jinja `
  --reasoning auto `
  -ctk q4_1 `
  -ctv q5_1 `
  -ctkd iq4_nl `
  -ctvd iq4_nl `
  -ctxcp 16 `
  -cpent 8192 `
  -cram 4096 `
  --batch-size 4096 `
  --ubatch-size 512 `
  --spec-type draft-mtp `
  --spec-draft-n-max 2 `
  --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 `
  -dev SYCL0 `
  -p "Explain in detail how speculative decoding works. Write at least 500 words." `
  -n 512 `
  -lv 3
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I am seeing excessive memory usage and a severe performance regression when using the SYCL backend together with `draft-mtp` speculative decoding.

This is not limited to a large 9B model. I can also reproduce a major slowdown with a smaller 2B MTP model when both SYCL and MTP are enabled. This suggests that the issue may not simply be caused by insufficient VRAM capacity, but may be related to CPU fallback/offload, host-device transfer overhead, or SYCL-side memory planning/allocation behavior around MTP / `GATED_DELTA_NET`.

I tested both PR #23174 and PR #23187, and both showed similar high memory usage / slowdown behavior on my setup.

draft-mtp is definitely active. The runtime output includes:
```
prompt eval time =    1340.41 ms /    28 tokens (   47.87 ms per token,    20.89 tokens per second)
       eval time =    9975.30 ms /   512 tokens (   19.48 ms per token,    51.33 tokens per second)
      total time =   11315.70 ms /   540 tokens
draft acceptance rate = 0.48456 (251 accepted / 518 generated)
statistics draft-mtp: #calls(b,g,a) = 1 259 259, #gen drafts = 259, #acc drafts = 158, #gen tokens = 518, #acc tokens = 251
```
So the problem is not that MTP is failing to activate.

However, when using SYCL together with MTP, memory usage becomes much higher than expected and performance can degrade severely. This also happens with the smaller 2B MTP model.

In some cases the GPU may still appear to have enough VRAM available, but performance still drops significantly. This makes me suspect that something may be falling back or being offloaded to CPU, or that there is expensive host-device synchronization / transfer happening in the MTP path.

With the same model, prompt, and runtime parameters, Vulkan does not show the same level of memory growth or performance degradation.

When using SYCL with draft-mtp, memory usage should scale predictably with:

- context size
- batch / ubatch size
- KV cache type
- draft length
- MTP temporary tensors
- GATED_DELTA_NET intermediate tensors

For a 2B model, enabling MTP on SYCL should not cause a severe slowdown if there is enough GPU memory available, unless CPU fallback/offload is expected.

If CPU fallback/offload is currently expected for some MTP / GATED_DELTA_NET cases on SYCL, it would be helpful to document that clearly, because the resulting performance behavior can be surprising.

I am not sure yet whether this is primarily a SYCL backend issue, an MTP speculative decoding issue, a GATED_DELTA_NET K > 1 issue, a CPU fallback/offload issue, or a memory planner / temporary buffer lifetime issue. However, since both PR #23174 and PR #23187 show similar behavior on my setup, and even the 2B MTP model is affected(Resulting in significant delays for the first token and a decrease in token throughput), I think this is worth tracking as an upstream SYCL + MTP issue rather than as a model-size-specific problem.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

 When enabling Native MTP (--spec-type draft-mtp) while using --fit-target , the MTP draft context is created with proposed max 262144 ctx reported by QWEN3.6 27B, instead of the fit-reduced context size. With 16GB GPU using an adequate small GGUF + reduced ctx like ~50K this eat some ~30k of the supposed available ctx. The issue is clearly visible launching the exact llama-serve script with Vulkan:

| Backend | MTP | Final `n_ctx` | Context [MiB] | Compute [MiB] | Context loss vs. no-MTP |
|---------|-----|--------------|---------------|---------------|------------------------|
|  ROCm    | ✅  | 19,456       | 544           | 37            | 72,448                 |
| ROCm    | ❌  | 91,904       | 245           | 37            | —                      |
| Vulkan  | ✅  | 69,120       | 544           | 38            | 40,960                 |
| Vulkan  | ❌  | 110,080      | 245           | 34            | —                      |

The "right amount" of ctx left available available with ROCm + MTP should be: ~55.8K tokens not 19,4k (~2.9x improvement on this test case). This is a huge difference for a 16GB GPU user, makes or brakes usability of such quant size.

That should be because:
 - CUDA/HIP (get_alloc_size) calls ggml_cuda_flash_attn_ext_get_alloc_size(), which accounts for F16 K/V copies proportional to  n_ctx. So flash attention workspace is counted upfront during fit, and over-allocating it directly reduces available context.

 - Vulkan (get_alloc_size) just returns ggml_nbytes(tensor) — the raw tensor size. Flash attention temp buffers are pre-allocated on-demand during execution, not during the fit phase. So the over-sized n_ctx doesn't inflate the memory estimate the same way.

Compute memory and --fit-target margin are the same yet llama.cpp's  HIP is overestimating required GPU memory by roughly 800 MiB when I use MTP.

items.body:
## Summary

Under parallel mixed load (`-np 4 --kv-unified`), `llama-server` on an **integrated HIP GPU** (Strix Halo / gfx1151, 128 GB UMA) returns **complete responses that verbatim belong to a different, earlier request**. A large-prompt request receives, as its entire response, the literal answer text of a short request from an earlier round. We also observed a **chimeric** response fusing tokens of two different requests' expected outputs.

**Bisected to a single commit: c7d87229 "ggml-cuda : restore prop.integrated on HIP builds" (#24233).**

| build | result (validated responses, nonce-checked) |
|---|---|
| 505b1ed1 (parent window start) | clean — 0 violations / 168 |
| 5839ba35 (= parent of c7d87229) | clean — 0 / 36 |
| **c7d87229** | **cross-request replays: 3 hard / 36** |
| e8f19cc0 (window end) | cross-request replays: 7 hard + 1 chimera / 96 |

The same harness against **CPU builds** of both window endpoints shows no build-dependent difference (model-compliance noise only) — consistent with the culprit being the HIP integrated-memory path. This presumably explains why it went unnoticed: discrete GPUs are unaffected; it needs an **integrated** AMD GPU (`prop.integrated == 1`), multiple slots and concurrent mixed traffic.

## Environment

- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo), gfx1151, 128 GB unified memory, ROCm 7.14, Ubuntu 24.04
- Build: `cmake -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang++` (Release)
- Server: `llama-server -m <model> -ngl 999 -c 65536 -np 4 --kv-unified --jinja --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'`
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE (Q4-class quant). First hit this in production behind LocalAI (same symptom after its vendored-llama.cpp bump crossed this commit); reproducing on vanilla `llama-server` rules the wrapper out.

## Reproduction

Load pattern per round (~30 s, script below): (B) short "repeat exactly this code: <nonce>" request → (C) large-prompt (~10k tokens) request whose system prompt requires echoing a per-request nonce in the first line → (D) burst of 4 concurrent short nonce requests (2 streamed / 2 plain). Every response is validated to contain its **own** nonce and no nonce of an **earlier** request.

On affected builds the round-N large-prompt request receives a literal foreign nonce as its complete response, typically from a round-(N−1) burst request. Verbatim from run logs at e8f19cc0:

```
R4/C got='pd-20260722-115649-3-d1'      (expected: reply echoing pc-...-4-c + a summary)
R5/C got='pd-20260722-115649-4-d2'
R6/C got='pd-20260722-115649-1-d1'
R7/C got='pd-20260722-115649-6-d1'
R8/C got='pd-20260722-115649-7-d1'
R3/C got='<!-- run:pc-20260722-115649-2-d0 -->'   <-- chimera: pc-...-2 stem fused with a -d0 burst suffix
```

In production we additionally observed: a poisoned slot re-serving its stored answer to unrelated requests **20+ minutes later** (the victim's `usage` then reports the foreign request's token counts), and occasional degeneration into repeated single characters (`/////...`).

<details><summary>repro-crossover.py (needs httpx)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Repro: llama-server cross-request response mix-up under -np 4 --kv-unified.

Each round: (B) short "repeat exactly: <nonce>" request, (C) large-prompt
(~10k tokens) request whose system prompt requires echoing a per-request nonce,
(D) burst of 4 concurrent short nonce requests (2 streamed / 2 plain).
Every response must contain its OWN nonce and no nonce of an EARLIER request.

Usage: python3 repro-crossover.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 [--rounds 8]

items.body:
## Summary
On the Vulkan backend, Qwen3.5-27B (architecture qwen35, hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full-attention layers) generates garbage / truncated output when the batch size is set to 512. The same model and configuration generate correct, coherent text at batch sizes 1024 and 4096.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11 (build 26200)
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (24 GB), AMD proprietary driver
- Backend: Vulkan
- Software: koboldcpp 1.119 (nocuda build, Vulkan backend) which bundles the llama.cpp Vulkan backend. The underlying kernel issue appears to be in ggml-vulkan.

## Model
- Architecture: qwen35 (Gated DeltaNet / linear-attention hybrid, full_attention_interval = 4, 3x DeltaNet + 1x full-attention per group, ssm state_size 128)
- GGUFs tested: Q4_K_M and Q6_K_M quantizations of Qwen3.5-27B, including a variant carrying the built-in MTP/NextN head
- Context: reproduced at both 32768 and 262144

## Repro steps
1. Load the model with the Vulkan backend.
2. Set batch size to 512 (llama.cpp: -b 512; koboldcpp: batchsize=512), ubatch 512.
3. Send a simple generation request (e.g. 'Write a short poem about the ocean.').
4. Observe output: random token fragments / garbage, or generation stops after 1-2 tokens (e.g. 'The.') with an early EOS.

With batch size 1024 or 4096 the same request produces normal coherent output.

## Notes
- MMQ disabled; Flash Attention on/off both reproduce the issue.
- KV cache f16 and q8_0 both reproduce the issue.
- MTP drafting on/off both reproduce the issue.
- The symptom pattern points at the Gated Delta Net kernel path selection: at small batch the autoregressive (non-chunked) path corrupts the logits, while at larger batch the chunked/fused path works correctly.
- Related: #20610 (Qwen3.5-27B garbage on Vulkan), #21888, #24812, #20515.

## Expected behavior
Output quality should be independent of batch size.

items.body:
## Overview

ggml_vk_get_cpy_pipeline only routed to the tiled shared-memory transpose shader when dim1 was the innermost dimension, i.e. ggml_transpose (a 0<->1 swap). A 0<->2 swap -- ggml_cont(ggml_permute(x, 2, 1, 0, 3)) -- fell back to the generic per-element strided copy, whose source reads stride by ne0*ne1 elements: one cache line per lane.

DeepSeek-V4's lightning indexer performs exactly that permute on a [n_kv, n_tokens, n_head] tensor. On Vulkan/RADV gfx1151 it ran at ~7-20 GB/s of a ~200 GB/s part and accounted for 43% of total prefill time.

Add copy_transpose_02.comp, mirroring copy_transpose.comp but tiling over dst dims (0, 2) with dims 1 and 3 as the batch, so reads walk src dim2 and writes walk dst dim0 -- both contiguous. The selection condition additionally requires a non-contiguous source and a contiguous destination so it cannot take cases the contiguous-copy shader already handles.

test-backend-ops only exercised ggml_transpose for CONT, so the strided path was untested. Add test_cont_permute covering (2,1,0,3), (1,2,0,3) and (0,2,1,3) over f32/f16 at tile-aligned, tile-unaligned and large shapes. The large shapes are in the eval set rather than only in perf because perf mode does not verify results.

Measured on gfx1151, ne=[n_kv,64,64,1], perm=(2,1,0,3), f32:

| n_kv | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 9.08 GB/s | 579.85 GB/s |
| 1280 | 20.03 GB/s | 153.71 GB/s |
| 2048 | 7.11 GB/s | 91.68 GB/s |
| 2304 | 16.24 GB/s | 86.49 GB/s |

The ~2.2x penalty previously seen at power-of-two n_kv (destination-stride aliasing) is gone. End to end, DeepSeek-V4-Flash IQ3_XXS prefill on a 9k-token prompt goes from 56.33 t/s to 103.74 t/s (+84%).

Note: at n_tokens=512 a single slow-path dispatch takes ~273 ms and looping it in perf mode can trip the GPU watchdog, so the perf cases use n_tokens=64.

Draft GPU layers: auto

Regression

b10353 works reliably with this configuration.

By b10470 the same configuration started failing. I also reproduced it with b10488 (9d77fa172).

The failure is:

radv/amdgpu: Not enough memory for command submission.
ggml_vulkan: device lost on Vulkan0
vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost

The kernel reports at the same time:

amdgpu_vm_validate() failed.
Not enough memory for command submission!

Sometimes the model fails while loading after a clean boot. In another test it loaded successfully and completed the first request, then failed during the second request.

Smaller models continue to work normally with the newer builds.

Workaround / important finding

While troubleshooting this with ChatGPT, we noticed that PR #26081 changed the default model-loading behavior for iGPUs between my known-good and known-bad versions.

I tested the newer llama.cpp build with only this additional option:

--load-mode mmap

This completely fixes the problem.

Gemma 4 26B + mmproj + MTP now loads and runs successfully on the newer build when --load-mode mmap is specified.

So on this Radeon 680M/RADV system:

b10353 default behavior                -> works

newer build, --load-mode auto/default  -> Vulkan device loss / command submission OOM

same newer build, --load-mode mmap     -> works

This makes PR #26081 / the new iGPU auto loading path look like a possible regression, although I have not done a git bisect and therefore cannot say that PR #26081 is definitely the cause.

Possibly unrelated warning

The log also contains:

Gemma4Assistant requires ctx_other to be set
failed to measure draft model memory: failed to create llama_context from model

However, this warning was already present in b10353 and in several earlier working builds, so I don't think that warning itself is responsible for this regression.

Additional information

I previously tried:

--no-cache-idle-slots
--fit-target 6144

Neither fixed the problem.

After a Vulkan device loss, subsequent model loads often fail until reboot, but I have also seen the original failure after a clean boot, so stale GPU state does not appear to be the root cause.

I don't personally need an immediate fix because --load-mode mmap is a good workaround for me. I'm reporting this because the clean good/bad behavior may be useful for debugging the new iGPU loading path.

TL;DR There's some prefill performance to be eked out for llama.cpp running on AMD Strix Halo. The changes are relatively straightforward, thankfully, but there isn't a clear "best" approach to implementing fixes ([this is just
what I did](https://gist.github.com/pedapudi/183f337e687630a43eacb293e157c9bd)), so I'll just report this as an issue. 

---

> **Pretext:** The following is looking to identify inefficiencies without being prescriptive on how to solve them. I'll share what I did, but I'm not saying it's the best solution. Happy to send PRs if the changes look good to maintainers, but again, I'm happy to defer to others for addressing an objectively large opportunity for this hardware.

> AI disclosure: Yes, for formatting, obviously (in fact, using llama.cpp). The writing is my own, but like most people, I don't remember the markdown format for generating pretty text ;) But really, please read the issue as it is written by me, regardless of how you feel about the formatting. At least it's not a wall of text!

---

Based on `rocprof`, I was looking to optimize prefill performance on Strix Halo. I focused on Qwen3.5 MoE models at Q4_K quantization because they're popular and amenable to performance optimizations. The resulting changes have been tested by a few different individuals in the Strix Halo community to verify the results. 

Overall improvement measured via llama-bench (with matching parameters) shows ~20% uplift on 122B model which really isn't subtle :) (subject to testing parameters). 

I'll summarize the areas of inefficiencies below.

## 1. VGPR pressure from settings in MMQ

There are three main parameters impacting this:

1. `mmq_x`
2. `mmq_y`
3. `nwarps`

All three are at suboptimal values for `gfx1151`. We can trace the code paths to infer how the values get set, but the more interesting detail is answering *"what should the values be?"* Static settings won't cover all hardware options, but for `gfx1151`, a **x=48, y=64, nwarps=4** provides a meaningful improvement. It's possible that further improvements are possible, including maybe via `__launch_bounds__`, or other values (although it's not evident if there's a better default than this proposal). However, the main point is that objectively, the current HEAD likely spills and exceeds the 256 VGPR (not all of which are usable anyway).

## 2. Leveraging intrinsics

> *Note: (a) and (b) are not specific to gfx1151, but the optimizations makes a noticeable difference on this hardware.*

- **(a) `expf()` → `__expf()`:** `__expf` is known to be faster but less accurate. In MoE routing (various lines in `gated_delta_net.cu`) and in SiLU activation (`ggml_cuda_op_silu_single`), the loss in precision does not appear to make any meaningful difference. Larger losses in precision exist elsewhere, and the speed trade-off from the intrinsic seems to be virtually free for the Qwen 3.5 35B and 122B models.

- **(b) `roundf()` → `__float2int_rn`:** `quantize.cu` executes rounding often enough that the intrinsic adds a noticeable benefit.

- **(c) `ggml_cuda_dp4a` in `common.cuh`:** Use `__builtin_amdgcn_sudot4` for RDNA 3.5.

## 3. Loop-invariant clean-up

> *Note: This is also not specific to gfx1151, and it's likely a meaningful code cleanliness change that also happens to have uplift in performance.*

At the risk of being prescriptive: consider declaring loop-invariant constants (`base0`, `base1`, `baseD` below) outside of the for-loop in `concat.cu:__launch_bounds__`. Given that this is the slow path, it appears to help clean up the code. What I don't know is why this non-contiguous kernel path is taken in the first place, so there might be underlying issues that I haven't figured out.

```cpp
const uint64_t base0 = (uint64_t)(i3)*nb03 + (uint64_t)(i2)*nb02 + (uint64_t)(i1)*nb01;
const uint64_t base1 = (uint64_t)(i3)*nb13 + (uint64_t)(i2)*nb12 + (uint64_t)(i1)*nb11;
const uint64_t baseD = (uint64_t)(i3)*nb3  + (uint64_t)(i2)*nb2  + (uint64_t)(i1)*nb1;

for (int64_t i0 = threadIdx.x; i0 < ne0; i0 += blockDim.x) {
    x = (const float *)(src0 + base0 + (uint64_t)(i0)*nb00);
    y = (float *)(dst + baseD + (uint64_t)(i0)*nb0);
}
```
---

items.body:
## Summary

On a Radeon Vega 8 iGPU (`gfx90c`, GCN), updating the AMD driver from 2023 to Adrenalin 26.5.2 changes the reported `VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::maxComputeSharedMemorySize` from **65536 to 32768**, with no other reported device capability changing. This costs ~17% throughput in Vulkan diffusion workloads.

Rolling the driver back restores performance exactly, and generated outputs are **byte-identical** across driver states — so this is purely a shader-selection/tuning effect, not a numerical one.

I'm filing here because `ggml-vulkan.cpp` contains an **exact-equality** gate on `65536` that looks like it may be unintentionally fragile.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | AMD Radeon Vega 8 iGPU, `gfx90c`, GCN, integrated/UMA |
| CPU | Ryzen 7 5800H, 8C/16T |
| RAM | 29 GB (3 GB UMA carve-out) |
| OS | Windows 11 Pro 26200 |
| Frontend | `stable-diffusion.cpp` master-796-2d0385b, prebuilt `win-vulkan-x64` |

`stable-diffusion.cpp` vendors ggml via the `leejet/ggml` fork at commit `eced84c86f8b012c752c016f7fe789adea168e1e`. I diffed the relevant block against `ggml-org/llama.cpp` master and it is **character-identical**, so this is not a fork divergence.

ggml device line on the **old** driver:

```
ggml_vulkan: 0 = AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics (AMD proprietary driver) | uma: 1 | fp16: 1 | bf16: 0 | warp size: 64 | shared memory: 65536 | int dot: 0 | matrix cores: none
```

On the **new** driver — only `shared memory` differs:

```
ggml_vulkan: 0 = AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics (AMD proprietary driver) | uma: 1 | fp16: 1 | bf16: 0 | warp size: 64 | shared memory: 32768 | int dot: 0 | matrix cores: none
```

| | old (OEM) | new |
|---|---|---|
| Driver | 31.0.12027.9001 (2023-03-29) | 31.0.21925.1001 (2026-05-19) |
| Adrenalin | 22.20.27.09 | 26.5.2 (Vega/Polaris legacy branch) |
| Vulkan API | 1.3.217 | 1.3.260 |

Vega hardware has 64 KB LDS per CU, so the 65536 report appears to be the physically correct one. 26.5.2 is the package AMD's own Ryzen 7 5800H support page serves, so this is not a mismatched driver.

## Measurements

Both runs were the first job after a reboot, preceded only by the SD1.5 job, so pipeline-cache and thermal state are matched. Same seed (42), prompts, steps, resolution and flags throughout.

**SD1.5, 512x512, 20 steps** (no flash attention)

| | shmem 32768 | shmem 65536 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| sampling | 80.12 s | 68.48 s | **−14.5%** |
| VAE decode | 6.84 s | 5.99 s | −12.4% |
| total | 88.42 s | 75.17 s | **−15.0%** |

**SDXL 1024x1024, 30 steps** (`--diffusion-fa --auto-fit --vae-tiling --offload-to-cpu`)

| | shmem 32768 | shmem 65536 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| text encode | 2.79 s | 2.68 s | −3.9% |
| sampling | 834.78 s | 696.14 s | **−16.6%** |
| VAE decode | 79.50 s | 65.63 s | **−17.4%** |
| total | 917.14 s | 764.53 s | **−16.6%** |

Output PNGs are byte-identical between driver states (SHA256 `BBEA8144...`, 1,907,961 bytes) — identical math, just slower.

The regression magnitude tracks how LDS-dependent each stage is: **VAE decode > sampling > text encode.**

## Suspected code paths

Line numbers below are from the vendored copy (`leejet/ggml@eced84c`, `src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp`); llama.cpp master has the same code at a different offset.

### 1. Exact-equality gate — the reason I'm filing (L3322)

```cpp
// On AMD RDNA, for small head sizes and big batch size the shader uses few registers, so too many subgroups get scheduled
// at once and end up thrashing the cache. Fix this by setting a large (unused) shmem buffer that reduces occupancy.
// This targets an occupancy of 4 subgroups per SIMD.
if (device->vendor_id == VK_VENDOR_ID_AMD && device->properties.limits.maxComputeSharedMemorySize == 65536) {
    if (device->architecture != AMD_GCN && n_rows >= 64 && hsk <= 128) {
        // 30kb target for hsk > 64, 26kb for <= 64 due to smaller workgroup size
        // Values are guessed, tested on RDNA2
        result.limit_occupancy_shmem = (hsk <= 64 ? 26 : 30) * 1024 / 4 / 4;
    } else if (device->architecture == AMD_GCN && n_rows <= 8 && hsk >= 256) {
        // Same thing for GCN, with an occupancy target of 2 subgroups per SIMD.
        // Here low-batch FA with large head size is affected.
        // n_rows < 4 switch because workgroup size switches from 128 to 256 there.
        result.limit_occupancy_shmem = (n_rows < 4 ? 14 : 26) * 1024 / 4 / 4;
    }
}
```

`== 65536`, not `>=`. The block has an explicit `AMD_GCN` branch, so Vega is clearly in scope — but any AMD device whose driver reports something other than exactly 65536 silently loses the occupancy tuning.

### 2. Shader-variant support checks (L3535, L3599, L10029, L10074)

```cpp
const bool supported = total_size <= device->properties.limits.maxComputeSharedMemorySize;
```

### 3. Division-derived batch sizing (L5265, L17468)

```cpp
const uint32_t batch_N = device->properties.limits.maxComputeSharedMemorySize / ((N + K) * sizeof(float));
```

### 4. conv2d path selection (L5450, L5483)

The cm1 and padded-shmem variants are disabled when the budget is too small. This is the best candidate for the outsized VAE-decode regression.

Items 2–4 are legitimate correctness checks — if the driver genuinely only permits 32 KB, they must hold. The open questions are whether the driver's report is accurate for Vega, and separately whether item 1 should tolerate values other than exactly 65536.

## Questions

1. Is the `== 65536` in the AMD FA tuning path intentional, or should it be a threshold comparison (`>= 65536`)?
2. Is there an existing escape hatch (env var / build flag) to override the shared-memory limit ggml-vulkan uses, for testing? I could not find one.
3. Has anyone reproduced a similar regression in **llama.cpp** proper on Polaris/Vega with Adrenalin 26.5.2? I only tested diffusion workloads; if LLM inference is affected too, the blast radius is much wider.

## Caveats

- Single machine, one sample per configuration.
- I have not built a patched binary to confirm caus

## Overview

**Co-authors:** @jxia4intel, @sliu39

**PR 2/3** of the Intel Xe optimization series — see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24408 (mega PR, draft) for the full feature set.

**Target platforms:** Xe-LPG Plus, Xe2, Xe3

This PR adds Intel Xe-specific flash attention optimization kernels for both ARLH iGPU (Xe1, UMA, coopmat1) and Xe2/Xe3. Dependency: builds on top of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24404 (Xe-LPG Plus coopmat1 enable). Independent of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24407 (GEMM+CW).

### Flash Attention (Intel Xe)

- New Vulkan shaders: single-phase prefill (`flash_attn_hdim64/96/128`) and two-phase split prefill/decode variants
- Pipelines keyed by `(head_dim, gqa_ratio)` for runtime dispatch across various GQA ratios without combinatorial pipeline proliferation
- Supports non-power-of-two GQA ratios via subgroup splitting (`qk_groups`)
- Intel Xe1 (integrated GPU, UMA, cooperative matrix) and Xe2 paths with separate warptile tuning
- Two-phase decode splits softmax reduction across subgroups; shared QK state copy (`fa_copy_qstate`) between prefill phases

items.body:
## Summary

On AMD gfx1151 / Vulkan / RADV, `llama-server` with `--spec-type draft-mtp` dies mid-**prompt** (`decode() failed: vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost`) at tens of thousands of tokens. The same argv with MTP off survives past 125k. A one-site diagnostic that **keeps MTP flags on** but skips `common_speculative_process` while no slot is `SLOT_STATE_GENERATING` also survives past 125k on both 1-seat and 4-seat topologies; generate still drafts.

This is not a checkpoint / `get_tensor` death (`--ctx-checkpoints 0`, this-boot `create_checkpoint=0` `get_tensor=0` `update_tgt=0`). It is not “Vulkan FA at 114k without MTP” on one seat (MTP-off 1×262144 finished 125948). It is the extra draft-context decode that `impl_draft_mtp::process` runs after every target ubatch on `!is_mem_shared` Qwen3.8.

`GGML_VK_MAX_NODES_PER_SUBMIT=1` is already set (the UMA submit-frequency workaround from #24872 / the turboquant fork). It is not enough.

## Name and Version

```
b10352-4dee52f82
Vulkan backend, llama-server
```

`/props` `build_info` = `b10352-4dee52f82`.

## Operating systems

Linux (AMD Strix Halo box).

## GGML backends

Vulkan (RADV).

## Hardware

- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (`gfx1151`), 128 GB unified LPDDR5X
- GTT pool 124 GiB (UMA frame buffer ~2 GiB)
- RADV / Mesa **last recorded 2026-08-16: Mesa 25.2.8** (not re-probed on the day of this write-up)
- Env on every arm: `GGML_VK_MAX_NODES_PER_SUBMIT=1`, `queue_preemption_timeout_ms=60000`

## Models

- `Qwen3.8-27B` UD-Q8_K_XL + `mmproj-F16` (Unsloth)
- Hybrid (`qwen35`-family): most layers recurrent, a minority full-attention. Qwen3.8 MTP is `!is_mem_shared`, so the draft context is a **separate** `llama_decode(ctx_dft, same n_tokens)` after the target ubatch.

## Problem description

With `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2`, long unique-prefix prefill dies in `vk::Queue::submit` during prompt processing:

```
radv/amdgpu: The CS has been cancelled because the context is lost. This context is innocent.
ggml_vulkan: device lost on Vulkan0
srv  update_slots: decode() failed: vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost
```

dmesg is a compute-ring timeout then reset (`ring comp_1.2.0` / `comp_1.0.1`), process **survives** as a zombie (`/v1/models` 200, later `/completion` 500).

Call site (b10352 `server-context.cpp` `decode()`, then `common/speculative.cpp` `impl_draft_mtp::process`): after every successful target `llama_decode(ctx_tgt, ubatch)`, `common_speculative_process` runs. On this model that is a second same-width draft decode. `--ubatch-size 1024` ⇒ a 1024-wide draft graph after every 1024-wide target graph, at rising `pos`. The outer `decode()` catch does **not** say which of the two `llama_decode`s threw; the A/B below isolates the extra one.

There is an in-tree TODO immediately above the call:

```
// TODO: avoid restoring the draft context and re-evaluating the drafted tokens when not needed [TAG_SPEC_AVOID_DRAFT_REEVAL]
//       for now, always re-evaluate for simplicity
```

## A/B (same box, same GGUF, same day)

Shared flags on every arm unless noted:

```
-ngl 999 --flash-attn on --ubatch-size 1024 --batch-size 2048
--cache-type-k q4_0 --cache-type-v q4_0
--cache-prompt --cache-reuse 256 --cache-ram 0 --ctx-checkpoints 0
--image-min-tokens 1024 --threads 16 --jinja
GGML_VK_MAX_NODES_PER_SUBMIT=1
```

Hop = `/completion` unique prefix, tokenized **~125948**, `n_predict=1`.

| Arm | MTP | seats (`-c` / `-np` / slot) | process() during prompt | last healthy n | result |
|--|--|--|--|--:|--|
| A | **off** (no `--spec-type`) | 1 × 262144 | n/a | **125948** | HTTP **200**, 992.6 s, 126.90 t/s, DeviceLost=0, `get_tensor=0` |
| B | **on** `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2` | 1 × 262144 | stock (every ubatch) | **55296** / 0.44 | HTTP **500** at t=6:16.751, `decode() / vk::Queue::submit`, this-boot `create_check=0` `get_tensor=0` `update_tgt=0` |
| C | **on** n-max 2 | 1 × 262144 | **skipped** unless a slot is `SLOT_STATE_GENERATING` | **125948** | HTTP **200**, 993.2 s, 126.81 t/s, DeviceLost=0. Skip log counts 1/16/32/48. Hop 2: `draft_n=6` accepted **2** |
| D | **on** n-max 2 | **4 × 262144** (`-c 1048576 -np 4`) | **skipped** as C | **125949** | HTTP **200**, 994.6 s, 126.64 t/s, DeviceLost=0. Same skip counts. Hop 2: `draft_n=6` accepted **2** |

Production 4-seat MTP-on **stock** process-every-ubatch (same argv as D, unpatched binary) died three times in the **114–117k** band (`n_tokens=114025`, `114688`, `116736`), same raise, same zero copy counters. Do not collapse the 1-seat 55k death into those 4-seat 114k deaths — same class, different CONFIG. Arm D is the 4-seat isolation: skip the extra decode and the 114–117k band is crossed.

After C/D hop 1, `begin()` warned `ctx_dft pos_max=-1` (the skip did what it said). Hop 2 was a short unique prompt, `n_predict=32`: generate still ran draft-mtp (`draft_n=6`, accepted 2). Accept is degraded vs a filled draft KV — expected with an empty `ctx_dft`, not a reason to drop `--spec-type draft-mtp`.

## Minimal diagnostic patch (not proposed as the final ship)

In `tools/server/server-context.cpp`, around the existing `common_speculative_process(spec.get(), batch_view)` after the target ubatch:

```cpp
const bool any_generating = std::any_of(slots.begin(), slots.end(), [](const server_slot & s) {
    return s.state == SLOT_STATE_GENERATING;
});
if (any_generating) {
    if (!common_speculative_process(spec.get(), batch_view)) {
        throw std::runtime_error("failed to process speculative batch");
    }
}
// else: skip draft-context fill during prompt. MTP flags stay on.
```

That is what arms C and D ran. A production-shaped fix is probably **tail-only / last-ubatch** process during prompt (so `pending_h` / draft KV is warm for generate) rather than skip-all. Windowed / smaller draft ubatch is another lever. `--spec-type none` is a diagnostic, not a fix.

## What this is not

- **Not** `--ctx-checkpoints` / `create_checkpoint` / `vk_buffer_get_tensor

items.body:
## Overview

This PR adds a **chunked mode to the Gated Delta Net (GDN) CUDA operator**, significantly speeding up prefill for >=128 tokens to the previous recurrent (token-by-token) kernel. All changes are implemented within the CUDA backend as a single GDN operator update.

The new chunked execution path utilizes a three-stage pipeline, inspired by the (vLLM) Triton/FLA GDN kernel, and leverages a mix of BF16, FP16, and FP32 to achieve throughput improvements via 16-bit tensor cores. This mode is enabled on supported hardware (NVIDIA Ampere+ with BF16 tensor core), otherwise original recurrent kernel is used as a fallback. The chunked kernel is GQA-aware and reads the fused QK and strided V tensor, similarly to the recurrent kernel.

Implementation in `chunk_gated_delta_net.cu`

1. **FP32 forward substitution (WY inverse)**  
   Computes intra-chunk corrections: `V_corr`, `K_cumdecay`, and `g_cum`

2. **BF16 WMMA masked attention**  
   Performs `Q @ K^T` with causal masking and cumulative decay

3. **WMMA state update + fused output**  
   - BF16 H-state GEMMs (FP32-range exponent prevents saturation)
   - FP16 GEMMs for `k^T · v` and `qk · v_new`
   - FP32 accumulation

### Accuracy

- Perplexity and KL divergence are effectively lossless compared to the FP32 recurrent baseline on the `qwen_3_6_35b_a3b_q4_k_m` model:
  - **Perplexity**: chunked 5.5201 vs recurrent 5.5052 (+0.27%, within error)
  - **KL divergence**: mean 0.0083, median 0.0019, top-1 96.8% — near-lossless
- To preserve accuracy, several safeguards are in place: the kernel handles g as a log decay by computing FP32 prefix sums and evaluating exp(g_cum[t] - g_cum[s]), which avoids problematic divisions by small exponentials. The recurrent H-state is maintained in FP32 across chunks, with BF16 only used when staging H-related WMMA operands. Additionally, WMMA operations use FP32 accumulators, while FP16 is utilized for K^T V_new and intra-chunk output multiplications.
- Additional safeguards: FP16 conversions are clamped to [-65504, 65504] and the output exponent for safety it capped at 88.72, and non-finite intermediate/state values are reset to zero.

### Addtional Memory

The buffers are pool-allocated and freed per op, so they're reused across all GDN layers and stays independent of model quant (always FP32).

items.body:
## Overview

We should now be able to add support for disaggregated prefill and decode to `llama-server`. For explanation of what this does see https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/disaggregated-prefill-and-decode or other articles. In simple terms, prompt processing is performed on dedicated devices/machines and then the decoding step is consolidated in a dedicated device/machine. The main benefit from this is the prompt processing tasks no longer interfere with the low-latency decoding of the sequences and can be automatically distributed to large set of machines in the network.

The main applications are in serving many users, but the functionality also has some interesting single-user use cases. For examples, owners of Mac Studio (fast decode) + DGX Spark (fast prefill) will benefit from this as they would be able to get the best of both worlds.

## Implementation plan

We should already have all the necessary components to support this functionality. I think the initial implementation should be completely achieved with changes to just `llama-server`.

Currently, we initialize a single `llama_model` + `llama_context` for both prefill and decode. We have to generalize this logic and construct more than one `llama_model`. Each new `llama_model` instance will be dedicated for "prefill" tasks and will use a custom list of devices. The list of `llama_model` and the respective devices are configured by the user.

The crucial point here is that the devices can be RPC devices. I.e., remote machines used for prefill will be represented as RPC devices with respective `llama_context`.

Next, we need to support splitting completions tasks into 2 stages: prefill task and generate/decode task. This separation will allow us to queue the prefill tasks to the prefill contexts. When a prefill task is ready, we submit the respective decode task to the main decode context (i.e. the one that we currently have).

When a prefill task is completed, we will store the computed memory (i.e. `llama_state_get_data()`) + prompt in the host memory prompt cache. This way the "decode" task can pick it up and continue decoding. Note that this step of storing the memory buffer to host memory will be performed over the network (for RPC devices), so fast network connections would be quite useful for these disaggregated setups.

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

this adds several fixes for rpc and rocm related GPU paths additional tuning and fixes crashes, prefill issues and general compatibility. Fixes #26746

### Included changes relative to upstream

#### HIP, RPC and long-context routing

- Enables hipCUB for HIP top-k and argsort, including the distributed RPC execution
  path, so these operations remain GPU-capable on ROCm.
- Adds a gfx1151-local Lightning Indexer top-k specialization for 512, 1024 and 2048
  candidates up to 8192 score entries, avoiding the expensive generic device-wide sort
  during DeepSeek-V4 long-context prefill.
- Keeps the Lightning Indexer key cache in F16 when a quantized KV cache is selected,
  where required by the DeepSeek path.
- Resolves fused operations per layer and device instead of disabling an entire graph
  on a single ROCm/RPC backend mismatch; the default fallback remains unfused GPU work,
  not CPU work.
- Fixes the HIP MMVF dispatch for MoE LoRA `MUL_MAT_ID` tensors. Rank-1 LoRA-B
  expert matrices now use the existing general GPU fallback instead of entering an
  MMVF kernel which requires an even K dimension; this prevents RPC worker crashes
  with valid DeepSeek-V4 expert LoRA adapters.

#### Strix Halo compute tuning

- Adds RDNA3.5/gfx1151 kernel and launch tuning for MMQ, MMVQ, Q8 MoE and expert MMQ.
- Caches MMVQ Q8_1 activations and partitions MMQ waves across rows and columns.
- Adds AMD WMMA Lightning Indexer support and tuned tiled Flash Attention, including a
  fix for NaNs in the compacted-tile mask path.
- Tunes Gated Delta Net and adds quantized-KV Flash Attention support for Strix Halo.
- Extends the gfx1151 MMVQ selection to the relevant Q4/Q5/Q6/Q8 and MXFP4 decode
  types, including the Q6_K VDR=2 decode kernel.
- Keeps HIP integrated-GPU host-buffer handling safe.

#### DeepSeek-V4 and speculative decoding

- Makes the grouped output-projection input contiguous for small multi-token
  DeepSeek-V4 speculative batches.
- Uses matching MMVQ and Flash-Attention kernel configurations for decode and small
  speculative/MTP verification batches, preventing numerical divergence between the
  logits used for acceptance checks.
- Keeps fused DeepSeek-V4 HC and Gated Delta Net operations on devices that support
  them while safely falling back only for mismatching layers.

#### Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 and hybrid SSM models

- Fuses SSM gate/beta projections, the SSM convolution-output L2 norm, and the SSM
  pre-scan chain (convolution, L2 norm, gate/beta).
- Folds SSM convolution-input concatenation into QKV MMVQ and fuses paired MMVQ
  matmuls that share an activation.
- Caches graph-local Q8_1 matmul inputs, folds Q8_1 quantization into RMS norm and
  gating-MUL, and fuses a matmul-plus-add-through-view sequence.
- Folds MoE top-k weights into the down projection and fuses the shared-expert output
  chain.
- Fuses IMRoPE and set-rows for BF16 KV cache use, and aligns the attention-gate
  tensor-parallel split with attention-Q.

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

tested on a halo strix cluster setup (RPC, rocm 7.14).

## Requirements

rocm 7.14, hipcub-dev (build requirements)
ROCm/HIP with hipCUB, HIP/ROCm >= 6.1.
Build for gfx1151 (-DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151).

OpenAI Codex GPT 5.6 Terra for tracing affected crash paths. Adding GPU fallback, instead of adding CPU fallback.

### Sources and provenance

  branch is rebased on the exact upstream commit stated above.
- [@Patt92](https://github.com/Patt92/llama.cpp) maintains this integration branch and

### Models

Reproduces on multiple, architecturally unrelated models — this does not look specific to any one architecture:

- `gemma4-v2` (gemma4 arch, both Q4_K_M and Q6_K quants)
- `gemma-4-12B-coder-fable5-composer2.5-v1.i1-IQ4_NL` (gemma4 arch)
- `Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-Q6_K` (qwen2 arch — plain dense model, no MoE, no known relation to DeepSeek/Gated-Delta-Net/Lightning-Indexer)

None of these are DeepSeek-V4 or Qwen3-Next/qwen35moe models, yet the crash is immediately preceded by `resolve_fused_ops` reporting several DeepSeek-V4/Gated-Delta-Net/Lightning-Indexer fused ops as **enabled** (not "not supported, set to disabled" as seen on other SYCL hardware in #26549).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` segfaults on the **first graph execution** (the built-in warmup pass, or the first real request if `--no-warmup` is used) whenever any GPU layers are offloaded (`-ngl` > 0), on this Lunar Lake iGPU. Model loading, tokenizer setup, and graph *reservation* (buffer sizing) all complete successfully — the crash is specifically in *executing* the compute graph, not building or sizing it.

`-ngl 0` (CPU-only, same model, same flags otherwise) loads and serves correctly, which rules out a corrupt GGUF or a general metadata-parsing bug and narrows this to the SYCL execution path.

Minimal repro (no server-side overrides, no third-party wrapper):

```shell
llama-server \
  -m gemma4-v2-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  -ngl 999 -c 2048 -t 4 -fa on \
  -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 \
  --port 8080 -lv 5
```

Isolation steps taken, none of which prevented the crash:
- `--fit off` (rules out the new auto-fit-to-device-memory feature)
- `--flash-attn off`
- `--no-warmup` (only moves the crash to the first real `/v1/chat/completions` request instead of the synthetic warmup)
- `GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_FUSION=0` (does not suppress the `resolve_fused_ops` messages below — that env var appears to gate a different, lower-level set of SYCL kernel fusions, not this graph-level pass)
- Reducing `-c` from 65536 down to 2048
- Confirmed with `dmesg`/`journalctl`, not just the process exit code:
  ```
  llama-server[86943]: segfault at 0 ip 0000000000000000 sp 00007ffd6a4b11b8 error 14 likely on CPU 3 (core 12, socket 0)
  ```
  `ip 0000000000000000` — a jump through a null function pointer — on every occurrence, across both builds and all three models above.

Only `-ngl 0` avoids it.

### First Bad Commit

**`5511965b197c131b38d8b5a0beb3ea7606d80b10`** — "sycl: route small f32 matmuls to oneMKL, bypass oneDNN" (#22150), merged 2026-05-18. First bad tag: **b9208**. Confirmed by tag-level then commit-level binary search down to a single-commit range (`e98bcfec2..5511965b1`) — see comments for the full trail and an explanation of why the diff produces exactly this symptom. Not #25806 as originally suspected here; that PR merged well after the actual regression.

Feature parity between backends is always desirable and it's easy to test the implementation, making it an ideal good first issue.

items.body:
## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.
